TCMax® can be connected to our LCD signature capture device. When you issue items to someone and have the signature capture preference enabled, at the end of the issue process you press the F6 key. Within a few seconds the signature pad will display a list of the items that you are signing for along with a cancel button, an OK button, and a clearly marked area for the signature. The easiest way to maintain the database is to use Microsoft® Access or SQL Server. However, we have included a screen that allows you to edit, add, or delete records. You can get to this screen by first enabling the edit features. Be sure you are logged in. Then click on the menu items Maintenance/Database Maintenance. Select the appropriate table from the drop down box and edit your tables as necessary. You may ‘drag’ column widths and the program will remember the width for the next time you select database maintenance.

Employee preferred assets allows TCMax to display the preferred items that an employee usually takes, such as issuing a weapon to an individual. You scan their ID card and the items that were setup in the Employee Preferred Asset Setup screen appear in a small table on top of the log/issued items table in the lower left part of the screen. Use this to find those items then issue them to the employee if they are available.

Many times you want to bring an item up on the screen for display or to edit the item even though you don’t want to turn in the item. Select this mode to quickly update any inspection requirements for any item. When an item is scanned that has a valid inspection requirement the inspection date is automatically updated to today’s date plus the interval displayed for that inspection. If there are multiple inspections assigned to this item then TCMax goes into the Edit mode and the inspections table is displayed. From there you can click on a single inspection and update it by clicking on the Update Selected button, or you can update them all by clicking on the Update All button. The computer’s speakers respond with “Inspection updated”.

When either of these modes is selected, items are NOT issued when scanned. TCMax updates the inventory date or special inventory date in the item table. These dates are reflected in four inventory reports and will show you items that have had and have not had an inventory within a given period. It also updates the quantity in stock. If the item has the “No Turn In” box checked TCMax will ask “Enter Quantity”. The quantity entered will be placed in the “Quantity in stock” value for that item. If the “Multiple items with this same barcode number” box is checked then the quantity in stock becomes the total of the quantity entered plus the total number of these items already issued.

This is the normal mode used for all issuing and turning in of anything. Once you switch to another mode of operation you can return to the normal Issue / Turn In mode by clicking this menu option. When you shut down TCMax and re-start TCMax, it always reverts to the default Issue / Turn In mode.

Select this mode to automatically update the current asset odometer reading or hour meter reading. *If you are a new user, please skip this section* When you receive an update to the TCMax® program you may have to make changes to the Database. Start your current version of TCMax® and click on the About button to display the version number. If the first or second number in the version changes then you must run the TCMaxDatabaseUpdate program. If the last number in the version is the only change then you do not have to run the Database updater. The updater utility is usually done by running Setup.exe. Before running TCMax®, click on Start > File Explorer. From the File Explorer window, navigate to the C: Soaring Software\TCMax or C: SnapOn\TCMax directory and click on TCMaxDatabaseUpdate then click the run update button. It will perform all necessary updates to your Database for the new version of TCMax®. The TCMaxDatabaseUpdate program will also update the Pocket PC Database. After installation, certain video card and computer combinations cause Windows to report incorrect screen resolution to TCMax® . You will know this because the main TCMax® display will appear to extend far to the right and bottom. Start TCMax® and press Ctrl + Q and a screen resolution window will open. Start by entering .8 (dot eight) in both boxes. Click Save and exit out of this window and TCMax®. Re-start TCMax® and make further adjustments as necessary.

When you place the CD in your drive a menu will start. The top button starts the setup.exe program to install TCMax®. You may just press enter answering each installation question to accept the default installation. Do not remove the CD from the computer unless you are very sure that the installation is complete by observing the TCMax® icon and TCS Label Maker icon on your desktop. This installation process installs the very latest Microsoft® Data access routines. The installation software sometimes must re-start your computer. This may happen two times on new computers. These re-starts should be fully controlled by the installation process. After the setup program has completed, you will have a TCMax® icon available by clicking on the Start Button, Programs, Item Control Software plus icons will be placed on your desktop. TCMax® installs by default in C: Soaring Software\TCMax or C: SnapOn\TCMax (based on version installed).

Many government and civilian information technology (IT) departments have increased security policies in place. To install TCMax® on those machines you must log in to the PC as an administrator before you start the TCMax® installation. Certain security policies will require you to edit the list of users after the installation is complete. Open a File Explorer window (right click on the Start button and left click on File Explorer). Navigate to C: Soaring Software\TCMax or C: SnapOn\TCMax Right click on the folder and left click on Properties If you see a Security tab, click on it. If you don’t see the Security tab, click on Items at the top of the window. Click on Folder Options then click the View tab. Uncheck the box that says “Use simple file". A list of the users is displayed, select the user required to use TCMax® or select all users. Be sure to allow full access to whatever folder that the Database is stored in (Access Databases only). If your security settings are preventing access to the folder, TCMax® will give you a fatal error when you first attempt to log in saying “Path/File Access Error”.

*Note*: Access is very sensitive to network problems. Rather than share a Microsoft® Access Database or place a Microsoft® Access Database on the network we highly recommend moving to Microsoft SQL Server® Express or regular Microsoft SQL Server®. When you plan to share a TCMax® Database on a network you simply move the TCS.mdb Database and its DatabasePassword.ini file to any shared directory on your network. If you have already started TCMax® before moving the Database, TCMax® will remember where the Database was. The Database location is stored in a file called TPath.ini which is located in your default TCMax® directory, (C: Soaring Software\TCMax\TPath.ini or C: SnapOn\TCMax\TPath.ini). You must delete this TPath.ini file then start TCMax® again. TCMax® will tell you that it cannot find the Database and then offer a File Selector box to allow you to navigate to the new location of the Database.

documents.t: Code 128 allows all of the characters that this software requires, and allows the printing of labels as small as .25” x .5”. However, the TCMax® software does not care which barcode type you use. The only requirement is that the scanner must read the barcode and send a carriage return.

TCMax® is designed to use any alphanumeric numbers to identify items. Organizations that will share items with others should coordinate the barcodes for items for these organizations. Duplicate item barcodes are not allowed.
Locations for item use can be entered simply by typing a location and pressing enter or tab. The TCMax® Label Maker may be used to make barcodes that speed the entry of locations.

This receipt printer can be used to print barcodes within the receipts (see example below). When you install this Printer Driver, open the Print Driver Preferences page for this printer, select the Additional Commands tab, and at the bottom of the page check the Cut Receipt [Partial] check box. The purpose of the barcodes is to speed the turn in process. The top barcode is the Employee Number. The second barcode are the words Turn In for a Location. The remaining barcodes are Item Barcode Numbers. Notice the Rag barcode in the sample above. Just below the Rag barcode, and centered in the receipt is a barcode that says minus nine. This person was issued nine rags. Turning them back in requires a minus nine to be entered, and that is what this barcode says. To quickly turn in a bunch of items and equipment the TCMax® operator simply scans the barcodes in the order that they appear on the receipt (employee number, location, and item barcodes with quantity when necessary), verifying that the item is there before scanning the barcode. You can also turn an option that prints a special barcode on the receipt. After verifying that ALL items are present, scan the top three barcodes and all of the items are instantly turned in. The Database used to store all item and employee information is in Microsoft® Access 2000 format and is password protected. The software is fully compatible with Microsoft® Access 97, 2002, 2003 or 2007. Reports that we have not thought of can easily be developed and printed directly from within Microsoft® Access. Each “item” has it’s calibration due date. There’s also an “Inspection” table for each “item” that tracks an unlimited number of inspection items for each. Any inspection that is overdue shows up in red in the inspection table. Expendable items can be issued with no turn-in expected. Checking the No Turn-In box for any item causes the program to respond to its barcode differently. With no employee on the screen, entering the item barcode number brings up the total in stock box. Here you enter the new quantity in stock whenever you receive new stock. When a valid employee is on the screen and the item’s barcode is entered TCMax® deducts one from the quantity in stock. If the quantity in stock goes below the reorder quantity then a label appears in red next to reorder quantity and the item appears on the reorder expendables report. Items that don’t need to be individually tracked but you have multiples of can all be assigned the same barcode number by checking the Multiple items with this same barcode number check box. You may often issue more than one of a particular item to a single employee. Checking the Issue multiple of this item with single scan check box causes an audio and screen prompt to “Enter quantity”. This defaults to one. You can enter the number of this item that you want to issue then press enter. This feature works both for expendable items (No Turn-in checked) or regular items that have the Multiple items with this same barcode number check box checked. Dates and currency values are all displayed in Windows® Regional settings, matching your local format.

Within a few seconds the signature pad will display a list of the items that you are signing for along with a cancel button, an OK button, and a clearly marked area for the signature. To verify the signature and that the spreadsheet has not been changed, click on the menu option Maintenance > Verify Signature on Excel Spreadsheet. By default, the TCS.mdb Database is in your C: Soaring Software\TCMax or C: SnapOn\TCMax directory. The Database can be moved and placed in any directory, including a shared directory on your network but you must also move the DatabasePassword.ini file to the same directory. Multiple Shops can run this software on their computers, all accessing the same Database located on your network. There is a file named "TPath.ini" located in your item control programs directory. This file must be modified on each computer to point to the location of the TCS.mdb Database. Start Windows® Explorer, navigate to the TPath.ini file and double click on it. You will see the following: 'The following is the path to the TCS.mdb Database'. Each computer must be told the location of the Database from the individual computer. Leave the commented (') lines alone. Change the last line to point to the location of your Database, Y:\LG\AGS\ITEM. This will tell the Item Control Software to look in that directory for the Database. Again, there is no limit to the number of computers or shops that can access the same Database simultaneously. The alternate method of telling TCMax® where your Database is located is to delete the “TPath.ini” file. The next time you start the TCMax® program it will tell you your Database is missing. Click OK then use the file selector box to navigate to the location of the Database. Double click on the TCS.mdb file and the new TPath.ini will automatically be created and updated. Wherever you move the Database, you must also move the file titled DatabasePassword.ini. That file must always be located in the same directory as the TCS.mdb Database file.

note If you purchased a Barcode scanner from Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. it will have been programmed before it was delivered to you and you can skip this section. For proper operation of the TCMax® software your Barcode scanner must be programmed to send a carriage return after all scanned characters. You can test the programming by starting one of your word processing programs such as Microsoft® Word and scan any UPC code from an inventory item. You should see the UPC numbers appear with breaks between numbers and without special characters. Example: If you scan 1239876 three times you should see: 1239876 1239876 1239876 If you see: 123987612398761239876. Then the scanner is not programmed properly.

TCMax® recognizes a number of sets of characters that will perform a task by scanning the Barcode rather than having to hit any keys on your keyboard. Example: Scanning a barcode that contains the phrase “clearscreen” will clear the screen just like hitting the ESC key on the keyboard. info Capitalization does not matter; these can be created in either upper or lower case. Print: Prints a receipt. Clearscreen: Clears the screen. Hall Pass: Prints a hall pass. Hall Pass - Excused: Prints a hall pass with an excused tardy. Tardy Excused: Marks the last student scanned as not tardy.

documents.t: If you wish to allow TCMax® to communicate over a network to a centralized SQL Database you will want to open the SQL Server Configuration Manager. documents.t: Create a blank text file and save it as a .udl (example: Connect.udl) on the Desktop of the client computer. Double click to open the file and then a Data Link Properties dialog box will appear on the screen. Connect to the Data Source. Click the Provider tab and select Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server. Click the Connection tab. Select the Server Name\Instance Name that the Database is on. Click Use a specific user name and password. Enter your Username in the Username box. Enter your Database Password in the Password field. Select the Database on the Server by clicking the dropdown and clicking on TCS (the name of the Database) or whatever your IT person named the Database. Test the connection by clicking the Test Connection button. If the connection was not successful then your IT person setup the TCS Database differently or didn’t setup a user as instructed. If it was successful then proceed with the following instructions. Please note that we automatically generate the Password by reading our encrypted version of the password out of our DatabasePassword.ini file. If you should choose to change the password then you must notify Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. and give us the password. We will encrypt that and send you the new DatabasePassword.ini file back. Or you can download our password encryption tool and create your own encrypted Database Password. Just paste the new encrypted version of your password into the DatabasePassword.ini file located at C:\Snapon\TCMax on the client machines. Click OK to close. Right click on the file you just created and click on Open With then choose Notepad. Delete the top 2 lines of text so only the connection string remains. It should begin with “Provider=” Copy this and paste it into our TCSSQLCONNECT.ini file located in the TCMax program directory. If you find this file named TCSSQLCONNECTsample.ini you must save it and re-name it removing the word ‘sample’ from within the file name. You may also want to check that C:\Snapon\TCMax does not contain a file called TPath.ini. If you were previously connecting to a remote (network) Access Database the TPath.ini file points TCMax® to where that Database was stored. You can simply rename it to anything other than TPath.ini and TCMax® will properly use your TCSSQLCONNECT.ini to connect up to your SQL Database.

Find and run the TCMaxDatabaseUpdate.exe file located by default in C:\Snapon\TCMax. Once the updater window pops up you should see Connected Via SQL Server at the top. Click the Run the Update button and wait until you see Successful-Click to End. You should now be able to connect to and run TCMax® off your SQL Server Database.

Once you have made a TCSSQLCONNECT.ini file and TCMax® can successfully connect to the SQL Server Database you can copy this TCSSQLCONNECT.ini file and drop it in all future TCMax® installation folders to connect all of the other TCMax® computers. The connection string will be the same for anyone on your Local area network. If you try to run TCMax® using it and get an “invalid connection string attribute” your connection string file was either created wrong or has become corrupted. The easy way to fix this is to simply recreate the connection string.
documents.s: Reuse your TCSSQLCONNECT.ini throughout your Base

TCMax® is designed to work with a single Database. Hopefully you have paid attention earlier and have actually backed up your Database. If your network goes down you can connect to one of your backup Databases if you like. You can later use the Import/Export function of TCMax to MERGE your data between the two Databases. With large Databases this can be time consuming, but it works. If you are using an Access Database and get an ‘unrecognized Database” error that is usually a result of a power failure during a Data write or a noisy network connection. Contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. immediately as we have an item that will restore your Database. When the network goes down you must have a fairly recent backup on your PC somewhere, along with a copy of the DatabasePassword.ini file. To connect to the backup Database open your c:\Snap-on\TCMax directory and delete the TPath.ini file. Restart TCMax® and navigate to the backup and continue to operate TCMax® as normal. When the network comes back up you can delete the TPath.ini file again, restart TCMax®, and navigate to the network TCS.mdb Database. To get your records from the local Database back into the network Database click on the Maintenance/Import Export screen. Connect the local backup as the source Database and the network Database as the destination. Click Merge again this may take a while for large Databases. All new LOG records will be placed in the network drive along with updating Stock records and Issued Items. If your network Database is SQL Server then you must periodically merge its Data into an Access Database, or have your SQL Server perform a backup periodically. If you have a SQL Server backup, simply attach it to another server and edit your TCMaxSqlConnect.ini file accordingly. Use the Merge capability of our Import/Export screen to merge the Databases back together once your network is running again.

documents.t: Taking your TCMax® Data from a Microsoft® Access Database to a Microsoft SQL Server® Database is fairly simple. You will need to be able to have both your Microsoft® Access Database and your Microsoft SQL Server® Database accessible from the machine you are attempting this on. The merging of Data itself will be done from within TCMax®. Step 1 will be to log in to TCMax® as someone who has permission to use the Import/Export screen. From the Main Screen of TCMax®, go to Maintenance > Import/Export. At the top of the screen you will click the Select Source button. This will bring up a window for you to navigate to wherever you’ve stored your Access Database. For this walkthrough I have my Microsoft® Access Database on an external drive that my computer recognizes as the H: drive. It is stored on that drive in a folder called TAS Import Data. So once I’ve navigated to my source Database the Import/Export screen will look as follows. Notice it lists the path that my source Database is located. Also, notice that two grids at the bottom populate a preview of your Data. The tools, equipment, etc. are listed on the left grid and the employees are listed on the right grid. The next thing you will do is select your destination. Since your destination is a SQL Server Database you will check the Use SQL Server Connection box under Destination. Normally you would see the destination Database’s information in the two bottom grids, but because our SQL Database currently doesn’t have any tools/employees in it the two grids will be blank. At this point you could merge based on a Shop Code. This is done by selecting the Shop Code you wish to import, in this example I am merging the default Shop Code. If you want to merge all of your Shops at once you can select ALL from the Shop Code drop down menu. Tools imported with our TAS Import program will have a Shop Code that is the first four characters of your WWID. So at this point if we click Merge two Databases based on the Shop Code, it will do just that. Merge brings over your tools and equipment and their information, inspections, and whether or not those items are issued as well as your employees. However, we can also copy all tools to destination Database, which will take every single item listed in your Database, regardless of Shop Code and copy it to your destination Satabase. The Copy All Tools button will not bring over your currently issued tools records (the tool(s) will come but it will not be issued out in TCMax®). If you are migrating an active Database with items issued out and you want to keep those records you want to use the Merge button. The Copy Employees button will copy all employees to the destination Database and the Copy All Log Records button will copy your log records to the destination Database. A typical install will want to Merge all Shops and then copy log records. The Copy All Items with Matching selected cell to Destination Database button is used to copy items based on a specific criteria. Example: We could click in the Source grid on a cell in the STORAGE column that reads Drawer 1. With that cell selected, if we click the Copy All Items with Matching selected cell to Destination Database button, any item in the source Database that has Drawer 1 in the storage column will be copied to the destination Database. It is important to note that on large Data transfers, especially log record transfers, the time it takes to complete can be substantial. If you are copying a year or two worth of log records it may take hours to complete. Once you have clicked the copy button and see the hour glass cursor just leave that computer alone until you see a message box saying the transfer is complete. Even if the program appears to stop responding or lock up your computer, just let it go until you get a message box saying the transfer was complete or an error message comes up and says something went wrong. You may also want to disable your screen savers and/or power down options on that computer to avoid this process having to start over.

documents.t: There are several versions of Microsoft SQL Server® on the market. TCMax® supports Microsoft SQL Server® versions 2005 and later. While Microsoft SQL Server® is available for purchase there are also free versions that Microsoft offers for those that don’t want/need the entire package. The free versions are called Microsoft SQL Server® Express 2005 and 2008. You don’t get all the bells and whistles with the Express (free) version but for those just starting with SQL it is the most basic version and has everything you need to run TCMax® successfully. Microsoft SQL Server® is a robust and versatile Database platform designed with small and large organizations in mind. The default TCMax® Database is a Microsoft® Access Database which is geared more towards home or small office usage. When running TCMax® you are essentially communicating back and forth with your Database. With Microsoft® Access, most of that communication work is done on your client (end-user) machines. What this means is each of those end-user machines need to have decent processor speed and RAM. The minimum requirements don’t change but it is safe to assume that the better your processor and more RAM you have, the faster TCMax® will perform. With Microsoft SQL Server®, most of that communication work is done on the Server itself. As long as you have a reasonably fast Server with a decent amount of memory you don’t need to have as much on the end-user computers. So by upgrading to SQL you should be able to speed up TCMax® without upgrading any end-user hardware. If you have more than 5-8 computers all connecting to one Database stored on your network, upgrading to SQL should help speed up each of the TCMax® users (issue/ turn-in faster, reports generate faster). If you use a Microsoft® Access Database over a network and during your normal use of TCMax® that network connection drops (either the network goes down, someone kicks a cable out, etc. any disruption in that connection) while Data is being written or modified in your Access Database, Access may corrupt the Database and you will not be able to use it with TCMax® until you use Microsoft® Access to repair the Database. So if you have network problems with connection being less than reliable it is highly recommended that you use Microsoft SQL Server® as it will not corrupt itself and shut down like Microsoft® Access. Microsoft SQL Server® may not be for everyone, however the simple task of opening a table and editing, sorting or viewing Data directly from the Database GUI (Graphic User Interface) is a bit more complex than it is in Microsoft® Access. You do not need to be a Microsoft SQL Server® expert to use SQL with TCMax® but direct manipulation of your Data from within SQL Server is a little different. There are also a lot more security features in SQL Server that your IT staff may need to address to comply with company policies.

documents.t: Introduction to TCMax® version 8. TCMax® is a comprehensive Asset Management and Item Control Software solution. It enables full digital management of toolboxes, workshops, and enterprise-level operations, ensuring that no item or piece of equipment enters the work environment without proper accountability. The system significantly reduces the likelihood of uncalibrated tools being used by personnel. TCMax® incorporates audio feedback and single-scan functionality, providing users with immediate confirmation of system actions. This capability minimizes operational disruption, as employees rarely need to refer to the computer screen; they simply scan the item, listen to the prompt, and proceed. The software is intuitive and requires only minimal training. By eliminating manual paper processes, TCMax® produces comprehensive digital records, allowing organizations to accurately track item usage, location, and timing. Configurable security levels offer granular control over user permissions. Administrators may allow individuals to perform all functions independently or, alternatively, require verification by another authorized user during item return processes. The system also supports the assignment of a single barcode to multiple identical items—each of which can be issued to different employees (excluding aviation-related applications). Although optional, the use of speakers is recommended to maximize the effectiveness of the audio-prompt system and enhance overall item-control procedures. Important: Do not let all of the features and the size of this user manual intimidate you. TCMax® has many features, most of which you may not use. However they are there just in case you need them. When you first setup TCMax® (or any time in the future) you can select features for your use. Looking through the feature list takes time. But, once you select your organization’s set of features, from then on it should only take two or three minutes to teach someone how to use TCMax®.

You can attach any kind of document or file to a TCMax asset as long as Windows knows how to open that file. The attachment can be based by Part Number or Barcode number. Press CTRL-A to assign an attachment by part number or CTRLB to assign an attachment by barcode number. Drag and drop files from the top window to the bottom window to assign the attachment. A copy of the attachment is made. When you display an item on the main screen with an attachment, the barcode number or the part number (or both) will turn orange telling you that an attachment has been assigned.

Use a part number based attachment when you have a single attachment that applies to all assets with the same part number such as MSDS’s or instruction books. Press CTRL-A and the attachment navigation screen opens. If you have already assigned an attachment (and only one for this part number) then the attachment will automatically open. If you have already assigned more than one attachment then you must double click on the attachment that you want to open.

Use a barcode number based attachment when you have a file or document that applies only to this particular item such as a maintenance record. Press CTRL-B and the attachment navigation screen opens. If you have already assigned an attachment (and only one for this part number) then the attachment will automatically open. If you have already assigned more than one attachment then you must double click on the attachment that you want to open.

CTRL-SHIFT-E brings up the attachment navigation screen which functions like the two above. This allows you to attach any kind of document to a particular employee number. The Employee Name lights up orange when that employee has an attachment.

Add new classes by clicking in the new blank row at the bottom of the table above. Enter your room number, class name, and period. Also, the number of minutes that they are allowed to be late and not be tardy and the number of minutes that they are allowed to be late and not marked absent. You also must check the day of the week that this class will be held in this room. Periods are setup in the table to the right. The Schedule of Periods combo box allows you to select from a range of schedules. It defaults to Normal. Other schedules may be 2 Hour Delay or 2 hour early departure. Periods define the start time and duration of classes. The period name can be alpha numeric such as 1, 2, or 3A, etc. Any class schedule line that does not have a matching period will display in red. Select a new schedule of periods by clicking the Schedule of Periods combo box and select the appropriate period. When you do this (and if this PC has authority to change the period for the entire school as setup in the Preferences screen) a new button is displayed titled Click to set this schedule for today’s classes. Clicking this button will tell all computers connected to the TCMax database that they should base the class start time and duration on this new schedule. This action must be performed before any student scans into a classroom. The action also must be performed the next day to reset the schedule to Normal as necessary. The Student Comments tab can be used to locate a student or maintain a history on student absences and other notes.

Start TCMax in the attendance mode. If TCMax is not already in the Attendance Mode then you must log in. The person logging in must have permission to complete student course requirements if TCMax is not automatically started in the Attendance mode. Scan the student barcode or type in the student ID number, TCMax says “Student” and places “AT” in the Work Location box. That is all the student needs to do! This action, scanning their student ID card will check them into their class. If you are also tracking the total time in class then students MUST scan their ID barcode when departing the class. TCMax will make a log entry that shows the total time spent in the class. If they fail to scan out then TCMax gives no credit for hours in this class for today.

Click on Student Maintenance/Class Setup, and then click on the Student Comments tab. Select the student name then click the Locate Student button and the following will show up if the student is in a class.

There are two types of hall pass, the regular hall pass and the excused hall pass. Hall passes are printed using a receipt printer. To obtain a regular hall pass the student scans their ID barcode then scans the “Hall Pass” barcode. TCMax will make a log entry that the student took the hall pass, log them out of the class, and print a hall pass with their name and other information. If an instructor should keep a student after class making the student late for their next class then the instructor can issue the special hall pass that will mark the student not tardy from their next class. To do this the instructor scans the student’s ID barcode followed by the special Tardy Excused barcode and the following is printed. When the student shows up to the next class the student scans the Tardy Excused barcode first followed by their student ID barcode. The student will be checked into the class and will not be marked tardy.

In Maintenance/Preferences you must first select the Courses tab then check the Check to Show Course Requirement Related Options check box. This also enables attendance modes Click OK to save the option. Note, if this PC is only being used to take attendance then you should check the Start PC in Attendance Mode check box. Attendance can be taken without requiring someone to be logged in. TCMax can also track individual tasks and the total hours spent on each task. To enable this check the Ask for a ‘Task Number’ in Attendance Mode”.

TCMax has an “Attendance” mode of operation designed to streamline taking attendance. The following instructions are intended to supplement the TCMax user manual. An example of normal day to day use is given first to show you the simplicity of the software. Instructions for adding students and setting up TCMax are provided in later sections of this document. To take attendance you first setup your class schedules. Each PC that TCMax runs on is assigned a room number. TCMax will attempt to match a scanned student ID with a class name via the room number that is assigned to this PC. When the student scans their student ID barcode TCMax will also mark the student tardy or absent if they are too late. TCMax automatically marks no one absent when no one show up for holidays or when school is cancelled for any reason. You can also use TCMax to print hall passes plus excused late hall passes. In the Student Comments tab of the Class Setup screen you can see the history of any student or find the current location of any student. The Other Reports screen shows the attendance history of all students including absences, tardy, total hours by student or task, hall pass history, and complete class schedules.

It communicates to the same database as TCMax. There are two screens used to setup the program. With the Email module running right click on the icon in the system tray. Use this screen to tell the Email module who to send email to and when the emails should be sent. Up to three shifts can be defined along with how long after the shift the Email module will look in the database for things not returned in time. documents.t: The Kit Builder screen helps you to build item kits or tool boxes. The kit builder screen is separated into three main sections, the search criteria at the top, items to be added to a kit or tool box are shown in the middle grid, and items currently in a specific kit or tool box are shown on the bottom grid. The search criteria fields; Tool Name, Part Number, Barcode Number, NSN, Parent Barcode Number, Serial Number, Tool Storage Location, and Shop Code, are used to filter the grid of items to be added into a tool box or kit found in the middle grid. For example, if I enter ‘320’ into the Parent Barcode Number search field only items that are in tool box 320 in my inventory will be shown, as seen in the screenshot below. The bottom grid contains any items already added into the tool box or kit that we are building. The Current Kit List drop down menu controls what is displayed on the bottom grid. As shown in the screenshot above I have tool box number ‘120’ selected in the Current Kit List so the items that are currently in tool box number ‘120’ are shown on the bottom grid. To add a brand new tool box or kit to your inventory from this screen you first must decide what barcode number you would like the box to have. The number must not be currently in use within your shop code. Once you have decided upon the barcode number you would like to use we enter that info into the New Tool Prefix and Suffix boxes. In the New Tool Prefix box you will normally enter the first four digits of your WWID or shop code identifier. In the Suffix field we enter the information that will be incremented when the new items are created. The data entered into the Suffix field MUST BE NUMERIC. If you enter anything other than a number into the Suffix field TCMax will ignore it and default to whatever was set up in the Preferences screen. If I wanted my new toolbox to have a barcode number J7EC600001 I would enter it like this: To add the kit to the system simply hit the Add New Kit button. You will be prompted at that time to enter information about the kit such as Description/Name, Storage Location, and Part Number. You can fill out this information now or leave it blank to fill out later. Once the new kit is added we see that it is selected in the Current Kit List drop down menu, and the bottom grid should be empty. Now we need to populate the new tool box with items. There are several ways this can be done and we will go through the easiest and most common ways to do so. First, though, we can choose to change how Kit Builder will assign barcode numbers to the tools in the box. Some will just let the numbers continue to increment using the same scheme, while others prefer to use the dash system for assigning barcodes to an item in the box. The dash system simply means that an item in a tool box’s barcode number consists of the tool box’s barcode id number followed by a dash and some more numbers to signify where in a specific box that item belongs. To set up the dash method of numbering the items in a kit you simply enter the tool box’s barcode number into the New Tool Prefix box, followed by a dash. And in the Suffix field you will enter the numbers to follow the dash. If you see below, this will cause the items in the tool box to be numbered starting with J7EC600001-001, -002, -003, … To add items to the new tool box we can double click on the item in the middle grid to add it to the bottom grid, or you can highlight an item and hit the Add This Item button. For the purposes of duplication an already existing tool box we will want to utilize the search features at the top of the screen. Enter the barcode number of the tool box to be duplicated in the Parent Barcode Number search box and hit tab or enter. The middle grid should be showing the items that are located in the box to be duplicated. To add the items into the new box you can add them individually or hit the Add All Above Items button to duplicate the entire box at once. When you do this, pay attention to the order that the items are listed in the middle grid as that is the same order that the items will be added to the new tool box.
Operation of the label maker program requires three basic steps Load or define the label dimensions. Load or enter data to be printed on the labels Print the labels

note Pre-Defined Labels Included with the TCMax® Label Maker Program A number of label definitions are included with your Label Maker program. Use them as examples to help you define your labels. When going from one type of printer to another you should only have to adjust left and top margins. There are many label material manufacturers and types of label sizes. TCMax Label Maker can be setup for any type of label on any printer that has a Windows® driver. We highly recommend the Polyester laser labels from www.barcodehq.com. They are strong, smudge-proof, water and heat resistant and available in many sizes. Their part number WP0571 is .5” by 1.75”, same as an Avery return address label. We also can provide custom polyester labels, for example .375 by 1.5 for special tool box inserts. Note the label definitions that end in “ESP” are for our Spanish speaking customers.

This is used to print inventory labels. The Avery 5167 is ½ inch tall and 1¾ inch wide. This is the smallest commercial label currently available that has adequate space for a barcode and two lines of text. When printed, your item labels will automatically have your message for top of label on the top line above the barcode. The label setup displayed on the previous page is for the Dymo® LabelWriter 330 Turbo that allows you to print individual labels quickly without wasting paper. See page 167 for a list of Printer Definitions and the numbers that should work for your printer.

This defines a label size used when printing sets of employee names used for quick entry with the TCMax program. It is intended to print on plain 8 ½ x 11 paper, not label stock. It prints barcodes which are to be made up of the unit designator (slash in the example) followed by the employee number. Put the employee name in the second column. You should always enter the number one in the quantity to print column. Use this same definition to print Locations.

Once you have your label dimensions defined you can load data. The left column of the grid is where you enter the information that the barcode scanner will read. The center column information is displayed on the bottom of the barcode label, right after the barcode number. The third column tells the printer how many labels to print of this particular barcode label. There is an item Search screen that you can use to select items.

Note: these definitions may not work properly with newer print drivers.

You can also select the barcode style which defaults to Code 128. This code handles alphanumeric characters well and creates a small barcode. You can also select the PDF-417 or DataMatrix 2-D barcodes, or other 2-D barcodes, however, those take a special scanner typically with an imager.

This controls the size of a DataMatrix barcode. Normal barcode imagers that are designed to read DataMatrix barcodes will require a cell size of 15 to 20. Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. can provide barcode scanners that will read much smaller barcodes. A cell size of 8 produces a 9 digit barcode approximately .1 inch square but requires our special scanner. When printing small barcodes be sure to increase the resolution on your printer’s driver as high as possible.

This box causes the barcode to be centered vertically but aligned along the left edge of the label. The Maintenance History Screen is reached by displaying an item or piece of equipment on the main screen then pressing CTRL-W. History is generated in a three step process: Enter a cause … a cause refers to the reason the problem was found such as during a routine inspection, special inspection, Advanced inspection, etc. Enter findings … findings are a description of the discrepancy or maintenance required Enter Actions Performed … this would be what you had to do in order to return the item or equipment to serviceable condition. Work orders can be printed to assign the work to an individual. A barcode appears on the top of the work order. Scanning this barcode from the work order screen or the main TCMax screen results in the item referred to being displayed in the maintenance history screen with the proper cause/finding combination being displayed. Then the user enters their actions performed. Below that you will find a complete history on this item. Work Order Sample A maintenance history report is available in the Other Reports screen. It will print the complete history of any item or all items issued to a specific person. The report is found on the Customer Reports tab.

documents.t: tip Backup your database on a regular basis. Backup at least once a week (preferably once every day). If you are running Sql Server or Oracle have your IT folks back it up daily. If you are using an Access database, you can use the F11 key or go to Maintenance > Backup Database to create a backup folder for your software. The first time you run this option, TCMax will ask you where you would like to save these files. In the location you select, a new folder will be created each time you backup, logging the date and time. Once you backup your system, you will want to copy the folder to another computer’s hard drive, to a floppy drive, CD-R, CD-RW, or tape.

The easiest way to maintain the database is to use Microsoft® Access or SQL Server. However, we have included a screen that allows you to edit, add, or delete records. You can get to this screen by first enabling the edit features. Be sure you are logged in. Then click on the menu items Maintenance/Database Maintenance. Select the appropriate table from the drop down box and edit your tables as necessary. You may ‘drag’ column widths and the program will remember the width for the next time you select database maintenance.

Before deleting LOG information from the database, make a copy of your database, saving it in a safe place. Delete your LOG data as necessary. To retrieve your old data, open the Import Export screen (page 103) and MERGE your existing database with the archived database. All old LOG records will be brought back into the current TCMax database.

Employee preferred assets allows TCMax to display the preferred items that an employee usually takes, such as issuing a weapon to an individual. You scan their ID card and the items that were setup in the Employee Preferred Asset Setup screen appear in a small table on top of the log/issued items table in the lower left part of the screen. Use this to find those items then issue them to the employee if they are available. To setup this feature, first check the Display employee preferred equipment in LOG table with employee ID scan” box in Preferences. Next, click on the Maintenance/Employee Preferred Asset Setup menu option. Select an employee name, then scan or enter the barcode number of each item that this employee prefers. They are added to the table below. To remove the item, scan it again.

Clicking Import/Export brings you to a screen that can be used to merge or copy TCMax® databases. The MERGE method is intended for customers that must monitor remote TCMax® installations. It will automatically merge Calibration Due Date, Inspection, and Quantity changes, always choosing the one that was changed last. It also adds all new records to the other database, in both directions. For Employee names and LOG entries it only copies data from the Source to the Destination database. The COPY methods are used to copy specific selections of records from source to destination. The Duplicate in Source method will duplicate a set of items using a different set of barcode numbers and a different shop code all within the Source database. It is used when an organization has duplicate sets of equipment spread out between large areas such as county response equipment, corporate facilities in other locations, etc. There are two databases that you will work with, Source and Destination. You need to select source and destination databases by clicking the appropriate button, navigate to the database and double click on the database.

Merging is based upon your “shop code”. If you have multiple remote locations that you will periodically merge their source data into your master destination database, then you should assign each remote location their own “shop code”. This shop code keeps the data separate in the master database. All database records maintain this shop code. If you manually enter data, be sure that each record gets an appropriate shop code. The source database will be a copy of a remote user’s database (by default this database will be a Microsoft Access® database named TCS.mdb however you may also use an SQL Server® database for either source or destination). In the above screenshot the source is a TCS.mdb (Microsoft Access® database) and the destination is a SQL database. Select the shop code of the Source database in the box just to the right of “MERGE”. Click on the “Merge two databases” button. TCMax compares the dates that changes were made to all STOCK records and updates either database as necessary. Then it copies all new employees from the Source to the Destination. Last, it copies all new LOG entries from the Source to the Destination.

Use this button when you want to copy all STOCK (item) information from one database to the destination. This is great when you are up-sizing from Access to SQL Server. The Copy employees and Copy all log records button will behave the same way, only with employees or log records.
documents.s: Copy all items to the destination database (or employees or log records)

documents.t: To create a duplicate set of data that can be used in a different location you select a Source database. Then enter the SHOP CODE that is to be duplicated, enter the New Shop Code that the duplicate data set is to be assigned to, and the barcode prefix and suffixes to be used. (Note, you are not allowed to have duplicate barcode numbers in the same shop code.) Then click the “Duplicate Items” button. The duplicate data will be generated, keeping the parent/child relationships correct.

documents.t: Use the Maintenance Procedures portion of TCMax to put together lists of items and equipment for deployments (see previous section). You create a fake “item” with the deployment’s name in the Item Name box, checking the Maintenance Procedure check box. Then go into the Maintenance Procedure screen, select this deployment, then scan the barcode of each piece of equipment that you want to deploy with. Later, when you scan the deployment barcode a complete list of this equipment is printed with storage location to help you find it.
documents.s: Deployment Planning using Maintenance Procedure Setup

documents.t: A maintenance procedure is a specific job that requires a specific set of items and equipment. You scan or type a maintenance procedure number and out of your printer comes a complete list of the items and equipment required for this procedure and where they are stored. If you have multiple shops sharing the same TCMax database and your shop is out of one of the items or equipment then TCMax prints the shop and location that actually has one available. And, if none are currently available then TCMax prints who has it and where it is currently located. See the example below printed on a receipt printer. The printed maintenance procedure includes the number and name of the procedure and part number, storage location, parent barcode number, shop code, and description of the item. It also will print the name of the individual currently using the item along with the work location where it is being used. The storage location will help locate the item from a cabinet or shelf. The parent barcode number will help if the item is located within another tool box or kit. The shop code will tell you if you have to visit another item/equipment room to find the item.
documents.s: How do you use Maintenance Procedures?

documents.t: Maintenance Procedure Setup is used to assign items and equipment to various Maintenance Procedures.

For maintenance procedures to work, for each similar item or piece of equipment you must ensure that the part numbers match exactly. If the items have different manufacturers and therefore different part numbers, make use of the Manufacturer’s Part Number box for the real part number, but place one part number in the regular Part Number box for these items. For example, use AN85088B for every ½ inch crow foot wrench, even if they are made by different manufacturers.

You begin by adding your maintenance procedures themselves just like adding an item. Type or scan the procedure number, it becomes a Barcode Number. TCMax says “New Item”. You type the procedure name in the Item Name box and other information as necessary. Before saving this, you must check the Maintenance Procedure check box located on the Purchase Orders & Misc. tab. Save the procedure (just like saving an item, hit the F5 key) Now you add items and equipment to this procedure by clicking on the menu option Maintenance/Maintenance Procedure menu option The Maintenance Procedure setup screen opens The combo box at the top is used to select each of your maintenance procedures. The table below shows you the items and equipment required for the selected procedure. Select the procedure that you want to add items to You can either enter the part number of the item that you want to add or enter (or scan) the barcode number of an item that you want to add, and it will appear on the list To delete items you can enter the part number or scan the barcode number or highlight the line in the table below and hit your delete key

Create a new item and enter either a part number or national stock number (NSN) and TCMax will attempt to look in its catalog for that part number or NSN. If found, TCMax will automatically load the picture of the item, the NSN, part number, and description if you haven’t already put something there.

One way new items can be created is simply by entering an item barcode number that the system does not recognize. A second way to create a new item entry is to click the Create New Item menu option or hit the F3 key. When you click it, TCMax looks in the database for the next available barcode number and then creates the new blank item with this barcode number. The top two boxes of this preferences screen tell you what that next barcode number will be. The prefix can be alpha/numeric. The default is blank. The suffix must be numeric. If you want your item barcode numbers to be all numeric then leave the prefix box blank. If you want your barcodes to be six digits long but want to start with the number one thousand then you should enter 001000 in the suffix box. If you want to use three digit barcodes and want to start with the barcode number one then you should enter 001 in the suffix box. TCMax automatically checks the database entry each time you click the Create New Item menu option, for the next barcode number. This way you can be entering new items from multiple computers and there will be no conflicts. If you should accidentally click the Create New Item option or decide not to enter it at this time, then you should simply hit the ESC key and the new item vanishes and the next available item barcode number is reset to the old number if possible.

If you have selected the Expected Return Date option from within preferences you will see a slightly different main screen. This is a US Army default. Note that the Employee side (left) of the screen has an additional item after Work Location titled Return Date. This date defaults to today’s date. Issuing items is very similar to the previous example. a. Enter an employee number b. Enter a work location c. Enter the date that you expect the item to return d. Enter item barcode numbers Entering this date allows you to view a report of all items that have not returned as expected

Select Preferences to enter your License Password, setup your employee barcode requirements, change screen size, or change calibration warning lead time. See (Setting Preferences for the 1st Time) for details on setting your preferences.

Main screen captions for instructions are setup here along with a number of buttons that set standard captions for English, US Army, US Air Force, Schools, Fire Departments, Railroad RCO and Maintenance, and the last translates all editable captions to the local language that is detected from Windows Regional Settings.

Change these items if your application requires you to issue items to something other than an employee or that the items are going to something other than a work location. For example, you may want to issue items to a Machine rather than an Employee. So you would put “Machine Number” in the box titled “Who or what is taking the item” and you would put “Enter Machine Number” in the box titled “First Issue Instruction (Enter Employee Number). This instruction appears at the top left of the screen, telling TCMax users how to run TCMax. If you want to track items by job number rather than a location you could change the “Where the item is going” option to “Job Number” and you would also want to change the “Second Issue Instruction” to “Enter Job Number”. Once these changes are made and you click OK the main TCMax screen will reflect those changes.

The English button simply changes the captions back to the original TCMax captions. Each of the other buttons U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, Schools, and Translate Custom Captions will change all captions and check appropriate boxes to fit those user needs. The Load Options from Network and Save Options to Network buttons load and save all options to the main database. This allows you to ‘clone’ the options to another computer easily. Setup your options the way that you want. Click the save button. Go into Maintenance and Preferences on your other machines and click the Load button. It will be setup like the other.

documents.t: This screen allows you to edit the captions for the Custom tab of the main screen. The main screen also has two combo boxes. The user can only select combo box values that have already been entered in the two tables that you see at the bottom of this screen. A special feature of the custom tab is a special wave file that can be played whenever an item is issued then the Checkbox 1 is checked. Included with TCMax installation are a number of wave files. Find the wave file titled UserCheckbox1.wav. You can use the Windows Sound Recorder to re-record whatever you want into this wave file. Then whenever an item is issued or turned in and the UserCheckbox1 is checked then this wave file plays. An example of its use might be to have TCMax say “Safety inspection required” when you issue or turn in a safety harness.

TCMax stores many options in text files on the local machine in the TCMax folder. Although these .ini files can be edited with Microsoft Note Pad we highly advise against it. In a few cases like those files that setup a path to the location of something, if you want to change that path you can edit the .ini file or the best method is to delete the .ini file then start TCMax and it will ask you to point to the new path. The following are some of the option ini files: CompanyInfo.ini contains your organization’s address, phone number, etc. DatabasePassword.ini contains the encrypted version of your database password (MS Access) or the encrypted version of your SQL Login (SQL Server). Displaydefault.ini stores your preference to display the duplicate button on the main screen. (Not recommended for long term use. If you must duplicate something turn the option on, duplicate it, then turn it off. It is too easy for someone that isn’t paying attention to duplicate items by mistake). MainToolsOutWidth.ini stores grid column widths of the tools out grid on the main screen (Ctrl-S). NetworkPath.ini has the path to item photos when you want to store them on the network. NewEmployeePrefix.ini stores the new employee prefix/suffix set in preferences. NewToolCtrlPrefix.ini stores the secondary new employee prefix/suffix. NewToolPrefix.ini has the beginning part of your new barcode numbers, along with the suffix or next available barcode number. Options_TCMax.ini, do NOT attempt to edit this file! It contains over 200 options and you can easily mess up many options if you manually edit this file. PDFPath.ini, contains the path where you want .pdf and .xls copies of your reports to be stored PPCInstallxxx.ini has several copies and are used in various PPC installer functions. These do not impact TCMax at all. RoomNumber.ini stores this machines room number when used in Attendance Mode. ScreenResize.ini is used to resize your TCMax screen when Windows fails to report to TCMax the correct screen size. This is created when you use Ctrl-Q to resize your screen. ShopCode.ini stores the shop code this computer starts up in. ShopCodeFilters.ini allow the listing of multiple shops for filtering. TCMaxPrinters.ini stores the printers that have been chosen for use with TCMax on this machine. TCSSQLCONNECT.ini stores the SQL connection string if TCMax is connecting to a SQL Server database. If you’re connecting to an Access database you should not have this file. TPath.ini stores the path to a remote Access database. This should not exist if your database is stored in the C:/Soaring Software/TCMax folder or if you’re connected to a SQL Server database. Xpath.ini stores the path to employee pictures.

The next two tabs, Employee Labels and Item Labels, define the layout of labels printed directly from the TCMax screen. Employee and Item labels have separate definitions. The definition shown above matches the requirements for a Zebra TLP 3844Z label printer and our custom destructible label material. When printing to this type of printer in the landscape mode you have to add a Top Margin that moves the print area to the left within the printer. The Barcode Type is also selectable. Standard single dimension barcodes as seen in the back of this manual are Code 128 which covers the entire alphabet both upper and lower case and is used by default. The newer 2-D barcodes like the PDF 417 and Data Matrix have built in error correction so that a significant amount of the label can be destroyed and the label can still be read. However, these 2-D barcodes require a 2-D scanner that can decode them. 2-D scanners are usually more expensive than 1-D scanners. The Distance barcode top to description box allows you to adjust the position of the description, below the barcode. It usually should be set a little larger or equal to the Barcode Height. The DataMatrix Cell Size box requires a number between 5 and 30. The default is 15. Smaller numbers make smaller barcodes. The number represents the small cell size of a DataMatrix barcode in mils. 15 to 30 can be used for normal imaging barcode readers. Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. can provide special imagers that will read a smaller DataMatrix barcode. The number 8 produces a barcode that is approximately .1 inch square for a 9 digit code. When printing small DataMatrix barcodes be sure to set your laser printer on its highest resolution! The Special item character text box is normally left blank. If you want all of your printed item barcode labels to be preceded with a special character that is recorded in the LOG table next to the employee name then enter the character here, anything alpha-numeric will work, but one character only. The Load Item Label button and Load Employee Label buttons offer the ability to quickly load our pre-defined labels.

You can print single labels directly from the TCMax screen. Select the appropriate printers with these three combo boxes. Your page printer is the printer that you will send all reports to. The label printer is where you print your individual labels. The receipt printer is only used if you print item receipts to an optional thermal receipt printer.

The shop code entered in this box comes into effect if the next check box is checked (Filter reports and displays with the shop code above). You only need to use these two items if you have multiple shops or organizations sharing a common database. The text box and check box are set individually on every computer. In that way any number of computers can filter by their own shop code, seeing only their own data. But any shop can un-check the box and see everyone’s data. A quality assurance shop may want to have the box un-checked while everyone else has the box checked and their own shop code entered. All item transactions are entered in the LOG table. The Shop Code is also tracked within the LOG table so that you see only transactions from your shop. When first adding items to TCMax it is very important that this shop code box be filled in appropriately. The shop code can be changed within each field later.

documents.t: Many TCMax users have separate organizations that share a common database. When you load items you can assign a separate shop code to your assets. This shop code can be used to separate log reports and keep from issuing items from a different shop. Some users will want to switch shop codes easily. Check this box and a combo box appears on the main screen allowing you to switch without having to go to this Preferences screen.

documents.s: Allow the options above to look across multiple shops

documents.t: The default is zero days. This number is added to today’s date when items are checked out. So, if you are packing items for a trip and you want a warning if any item will go out of calibration or overdue inspection during the trip, set this number to the number of days from now until the end of the trip. Any item scanned after the preferences are saved will cause a “Calibration Imminent” warning to fire if the calibration due date is before the end of your trip. To disable this feature, set the days to zero. You will get an “Overdue Calibration” warning if the item is actually overdue.
documents.s: Warning lead time in days for Calibrations

documents.t: This works just like calibrations above except it monitors inspection dates and will give you an “Inspection Imminent” audio warning telling you that something is expiring within the period of now plus the number of days in this box.
documents.s: Warning lead time in days for Inspections

documents.t: With this checked, and when you scan a barcode that should be a work location, TCMax warns you with “Attention” if you should accidentally scan an item barcode prompting you to scan a work location barcode.
documents.s: Check to make sure work locations are not item barcodes

documents.t: Check this box and you turn on the ability to set a default location for individual employees. When set, the employee simply enters his or her employee number, the default location automatically appears, and they are ready to issue items to that location. To set a default location, enter an employee number and enter a location as normal. The Set Default button appears just to the right of the Location text box. Click the button, the default is set, and the button changes to Un-Set Default. To un-set the default location for this employee, just click the Un-Set Default button.
documents.s: Show Button and enable setting of default locations for individual employees

documents.t: Checking this option gives you the ability to have a set of alternate work locations when turning in items. You can type in how you want the caption to display on the Captions 2 tab in Preferences. You can also have TCMax play a different audio file for this. With this checked, a grid will appear where you can type in the alternate work locations to use for the turn-in process. You can also force that only the work locations entered in the grid are the ones used and not allow blank work locations for turning in items.
documents.s: Display Alternate Work Location for Turn In

documents.t: Enter your work locations in the table to the left, building numbers, job numbers, aircraft tail numbers, etc. From the main screen, enter your employee number, when TCMax is looking for your work location a screen full of large buttons shows up. You can touch one of the buttons, click it with a mouse, type your own location, or scan a location barcode; they all work to capture a work location.

documents.s: Do not ask for Work Location when issuing items

documents.t: When using this, after you enter an employee number, the cursor will be in between whatever is input for the prefix and suffix boxes for this option in the work location field.
documents.s: Add Prefix and Suffix to Work Location

documents.t: When checked and you start TCMax, TCMax will ask you to log in immediately.
