documents.s: Automatically clear Employee Numbers after selected number of minutes

documents.t: With this box checked when you hit the F4 key from the main screen a new employee number is automatically generated, TCMax says “New Employee” and you can type the employee name and hit enter to save it.
documents.s: Enable F4 key for new employees

documents.t: Check this box to remove all employee numbers from the main screen (default).
documents.s: Hide Employee Numbers on main screen

documents.t: Check this to display the shift (1, 2, or 3, for first shift, second shift, third shift) that this person is supposed to be working and the name of their organization. This information also appears in the Show Items that are Out screen. Also, in the upper right corner of the screen, the current shift is displayed. You must change the shift by clicking on this combo box and selecting the current shift. If you attempt to issue items to someone that is assigned to a different shift, TCMax will first say “Attention”, and then it says “Issue” as necessary.
Before anyone can view any reports they have to be given permissions through the Maintenance/Set Employee access permissions screen.
documents.s: Restrict reports to those with permission

documents.t: When you check this box TCMax will ask for the main database password so that only a limited few will be able to change this option. When checked a box opens to the right where you set the number of days between mandatory password changes. Also, another box opens up asking for the Minimum Password Length. With this option turned on full password integrity will be enforced, meaning that every password will require at least one lower case letter, one upper case letter, one number, and one special character. This will be checked whenever someone changes their password. When the TCMax operator logs in we will check to see when their password was last changed and if it exceeds the maximum number of days TCMax will ask for a new password, and it will ask you to repeat that password. We then check to verify there are enough characters and that they have proper integrity. If any of those items fail then you will not be logged in.
documents.s: Force employees to change their password after selected number of days

documents.t: This allows you to always be logged in to TCMax when you are logged in to your computer. This feature works with CAC (Common Access Card) cards as well. When you enable this feature in TCMax then restart TCMax for the first time and log in with your TCMax ID, it will remember the Windows Login ID that you signed in with. Anytime TCMax is started and you are logged in to Windows, you will also be logged into TCMax, employee name on the screen for issuing to, and either the Work Location question displayed or ready to issue tools depending on your other options settings.
documents.s: Link Windows ID to TCMax ID

documents.t: As it says, prevent someone from issuing a tool box that has overdue items or items that were previously issued.
documents.s: Do not allow a parent to be issued if it has missing/overdue children

documents.t: With this box checked TCMax will refuse to issue items that are overdue inspection unless you have permission to change a calibration due date.
documents.s: Restrict the issue of items that are overdue an inspection

documents.t: This is not a suggested option for normal use. If you issue a parent, its children and grandchildren will get issued too.
documents.s: When issuing a parent, automatically issue its children and grandchildren

documents.t: This option when checked will cause TCMax to automatically ask you to issue children upon the turn in of the parent, but only children with ‘drawer’ in the beginning of the name. This is used when you want your employees to be forced to open every drawer of their tool box when turning it in. You barcode the back of each drawer. When the box is turned in, the drawers are issued (if you answer Yes) and they have to open every drawer, scanning the drawer barcode to turn each back in, hopefully spotting any missing items during this process. The name of the item (description) must begin with the word “Drawer” (i.e. Drawer 1, DRAWER 2, drawer 8, etc.) and it must have the parent barcode number of the tool box.
documents.s: Automatically issue children when a parent is turned in for an item with ‘Drawer’ in the name

documents.t: This stops you from issuing children separately out of an item kit. This probably should remain unchecked except in very special cases.
documents.s: Do not allow Children to be issued

documents.t: Check this box and when you issue something with the custom fields User Checkbox number 3 checked TCMax will ask you for the password of the employee that is receiving the items or equipment. It will do this only for the first item in this issue session that has the use checkbox 3 checked. We recommend changing the caption of this checkbox to “Password Required” when you use this option.
documents.s: Ask for Password with User checkbox 3

documents.t: Check this box and a small box will open to the right. Enter the maximum number of items in this box. When you issue more than this number of items to a single employee TCMax will say “Attention” warning you but the items will be issued anyway.
documents.s: Limit the number of items an employee can have issued at one time

documents.t: Check this box and a small box will open to the right. Enter the maximum number of items in the box. An employee will not be able to be issued more than this amount of tools that share a part number. When you issue more than this number of items to a single employee TCMax will say “Attention” warning you but the items will be issued anyway.
documents.s: Limit the number of tools (of a particular part number) an employee can have issued at one time

documents.t: This is a US Navy requirement. When an item is issued they must place an item tag next to the storage place for the item. With TCMax you first issue the item then TCMax expects you to issue one of your item tags. Item tags are added to the TCMax database exactly like adding an item, except you must check the Item Tag (Item Chit) check box.
documents.s: Force users to scan an item Tag after each item

documents.t: With this option turned on TCMax adds one additional step when issuing items, asking for a control number. The issue process becomes: Employee number Work Location (optionally) Control Number Return Date (optionally)
documents.s: Ask for a ‘Control Number’ when issuing items

documents.t: This option was designed to meet U.S. Army regulations. It adds the requirement to enter an expected item return date after entering an Employee number and a Work Location. It allows you to monitor items that are to be issued for more than one day and warn you via a report when items have not been returned by that expected return date. When issuing items with a calibration or inspection due date TCMax will compare your return date to those due dates and warn you if it will go overdue while you’re expected to have it issued out.
documents.s: Ask for ‘Expected Return Date’ when entering Employee / Location

documents.t: The expected return date (if turned on) defaults to today. Some customers want that defaulted to some other time in the future. Enter the number of days from today.
documents.s: Number of days from today for default ‘Expected Return Date’

documents.t: If the employee has items that are overdue turn in (return date option must be turned on) then TCMax says “Attention” and will not allow you to issues until they return their overdue items.
documents.s: Do not allow items to be issued to an employee with overdue returns

documents.t: When not checked TCMax assumes that if you issue a quantity of items that you must have the items in hand and know that they are there. If the inventory count in TCMax says you don’t have enough it still issues them. When you check this box, and TCMax thinks that you don’t have enough, then TCMax says “Attention” and tells you that there are not enough available.
documents.s: Do not allow issue when there are not enough in stock

documents.t: If the majority of your items are allowed to have multiple items with the same barcode number and therefore allowed to be issued to multiple employees under a single item barcode number then you should check this box. When new items are created the Multiple items with this same barcode number box will automatically be checked.
documents.s: Default new items to have multiple items with the same barcode number

documents.t: If the majority of your items are issued in quantities of more than one at a time then check this box. When new items are created the Issue multiple of this item with single scan check box will automatically be checked for you.
documents.s: Default new items to allow multiple issue with single scan

documents.t: If checked, this option will force the employee selection list to appear to select who the items that are being scanned are turned in from.
documents.s: Always display selection list for multiple items with the same barcode number

documents.t: This option when checked is used in a manufacturing environment where you may take a quantity of items on the job with the intention of leaving some or all on the job. For example, in an aircraft manufacturing plant you take 50 bolts on the aircraft. 45 of them are used in the aircraft to bolt things together, and will stay there for the life of the aircraft. When you leave the aircraft you take the five extra ones out and turn them in. When you scan the barcode number for the bolts you enter -5 (minus five) to turn those five in. With this box checked TCMax will say “Attention” and a prompt will ask you if the “other 45 have been consumed on the job.” If you click Yes then the other 45 are removed from the issued items list, and a separate Log entry is made showing their consumption. These ‘consumed’ items will appear on the special “Customer” Consumable Use Log report.
documents.s: Consume option when multiple turn-in is short

documents.t: As it says, you do not need to be logged in to issue items, but you must be logged in to turn things in.
documents.s: Do not allow turn in unless someone is logged in

documents.t: With this option checked, the person who is logged into TCMax will not be able to turn in items that are issued to their employee number.
documents.s: Person logged in cannot turn in their own items

documents.t: Other people cannot turn in your items, only you can turn in your items.

documents.t: This option when not checked allows a person to check in his or her own items. When checked, if a person tries to check in their own items a warning audio is heard “Second Person Required for Turn-In” and the item is not turned in.

documents.t: Checking this box prevents items from being turned in when you want them displayed on the screen, but have no employee/location combination on the screen. Without the box being checked you can turn things in without an employee name.

documents.s: Prompt before turning someone else’s items in

documents.t: By default this box is checked. If you should accidentally issue the wrong item, scanning it again right away turning it back in causes the LOG record for that issue to be deleted. This keeps your usage records to be more accurate.
documents.s: If an item is turned in within one minute of it being issued, delete its original log record

documents.t: As the title suggests, when you turn in the keys for a vehicle, TCMax will ask you to enter the current miles or hours to keep that updated easily.

documents.t: All items that are turned in on a computer with this item checked will have their storage location changed to whatever is typed in the Default storage location box. In this instance the storage location for all items turned in using this computer will have their storage location changed to Toolbox 100.

documents.t: This is not a suggested option for normal use. When performing a Physical Inventory, if you enter a quantity for a multiple quantity item that is less than what TCMax shows, the Qty on Hand for that item will be changed to reflect the lesser quantity. For example, if the item shows as having a quantity of 20, but when the physical inventory is done there are only 15, the quantity for that item in TCMax will be changed to reflect 15.
documents.s: When in Physical Inventory Mode, adjust ‘Quantity on Hand’ when multiple item quantity is short

documents.t: The Inventory Date field in the Stock table is also updated when any barcode is scanned while in the Physical Inventory mode. This makes better use of the inventory reports.
documents.s: Update Inventory Date when in Physical Inventory mode and an item is turned in

documents.t: There are times that you want to issue expendable items but when doing a physical inventory be prompted to replenish those expendable items back up to the max in stock value. This turns that ability on.
documents.s: Physical Inventory Mode uses Max in Stock value for ‘Issue Multiple’ items instead of Qty on Hand

documents.s: Enable color prompts for issue and turn-in on the main screen

documents.t: The Quick Turn @ Shift Change menu item is used when you have a multi-shift operation and want to allow items to be transferred without actually scanning each individual item. It allows you to pick all items issued to an individual or to a location and transfer them to the employee already on the main screen.

You can add that exact item (with a different barcode number) to another shop code with a single click. Also displayed is another button Duplicate X Times button. Bring up an item on the main screen, click the button and TCMax will ask you how many duplicates you want. Enter something other than zero and TCMax will use the next available barcode number and add the appropriate duplicates to the database with new barcode numbers. TCMax will also ask you if you want labels printed.

documents.t: Examples will be crimping items, go/no go gauges, you may have to do an inspection based on the number of times the item is used. Check this box, the captions for Current Miles change to Total Times Used. When the item is turned in TCMax will say “Attention” then ask you to enter the number of times this item was used during this issue period. That number is added to the Total Times Used, and then the inspections are tested to see if any are overdue. You enter the number of total uses for the next inspection in the Uses Due column of the inspection table. You can also setup an interval in the Uses Interval column that is used during the Inspection Update mode. Note: the item’s Total Times Used must be greater than zero for this to function.
documents.s: Ask for the number of times this item was actually used

documents.t: When checked, and when you click the Print Item Label button, TCMax will ask you how many labels you want, defaulting to one.

documents.t: With this option enabled and with our LCD signature pad attached to your PC you can capture an electronic signature. After you issue items to someone you hit the F6 key. A list of the items issued to the person within the last two hours will be displayed on the PC screen and the LCD signature pad. The employee signs for the items and clicks the OK button on the LCD signature pad. From that we double encrypt the signature; the second encryption key is based on a list of the items that the person is signing for. The signature is then embedded in an Excel spreadsheet which is immediately saved using the employee name and the date and time. To later view the Excel spreadsheet and verify that nothing has been edited within the saved spreadsheet you click on Maintenance/Verify Signature on Excel Spreadsheet. You navigate to the spreadsheet and open it. If nothing has been changed, you will see the signature appear.
Sign for the item and TCMax clears the main screen.
documents.s: Automatically clear employee names off the screen after a signature has been captured

documents.t: Check this box if you have already installed our fingerprint reader and software.

This option defaults to “4”. In random mode, each time that you start TCMax the program randomly picks one of the first six sets of wave files to use to say the words “Issue” and “Turn In”, etc. You can force TCMax to use only one of the sets of files each time you start by selecting a number from 1 to 6. Then you can rely on TCMax choosing that set if files with each start. The files are titled “Issu1.wav”, “Issu2.wav”, etc. The number that you select in this option will match the number in the wave file. Additional Wave File Languages: Spanish French Italian German Mandarin You are welcome to use the Windows Sound Recorder to re-record any of these wave files to fit your needs. If you re-record them be sure to clip the leading and trailing space from the files, to keep them as short as possible.
documents.s: Wave files ending with this number are used

documents.t: This option will take over the comm port typically assigned to 2D serial scanners and allow specific IdentityOne Biometric readers to pass credentials to TCMax.

TCMax can communicate with a serial barcode scanner. This requires a COMM Port to be entered. To disable the Serial Barcode Scanner: Enter a 0 (zero) in the box. To enable the Serial Barcode Scanner: Determine your COMM Port Note: To determine the COMM port number you must first have a serial port that you will hook your lock to. If your computer doesn’t have a serial port, install a USB to Serial adapter. a. Click on the Start button b. Click on Control Panel c. Double-Click the System icon d. Click the Hardware tab e. Click the Device Manager button f. Click the + next to Ports (COM & LPT) Next to your COMM port you will see the port number. Enter your COMM port number into the COMM port number box in TCMax. Now, each time you start TCMax communications the port will be tested. If the communications fail, TCMax will warn you, disable the port software, and continue to work normally without lock communications.
documents.s: Comm port number for Serial 2-D barcode scanner

documents.t: TCMax has the ability to communicate with a serial lock mechanism that when unlocked will automatically place the employee number on the screen of the person that opened the lock. This requires a Comm Port to be entered. Enter a 0 (zero) to disable this feature. To determine the Comm port number you must first have a serial port that you will hook your lock to. If your computer doesn’t have a serial port, install a USB to Serial adapter. Then perform the following steps to find your Comm port number. a. Click on the Start button b. Click on Control Panel c. Click the System icon d. Click the Hardware tab e. Click the Device Manager button f. Click the + next to Ports (COM & LPT) Next to your COMM port you will see the port number. Enter this in the Comm port number box. Each time you start TCMax, communications with the port will be tested. If the communications fails, TCMax will warn you, disable the port software, and continue to work normally without lock communications.
documents.s: Comm port number for Serial Port Lock Mechanism

Part one is any text which can be the description; second part is the barcode number; third part is the calibration date that must be in the local regional date format.

When enabling the US Navy HazMat option on the Preferences General Req 5 tab, your item will be affected by the following fields in the tool information window on the main screen: HazMat Max Weight field on the Purchase Orders & Misc tab, HazMat checkbox, Is Disposable checkbox and Current Weight on the Custom tab. After checking the US Navy Hazmat options in General Req 5, to indicate an item is a HazMat item, the HazMat checkbox in the Custom tab of the tool information must be checked. The weight of the item will now be tracked by TCMax in the Current Weight box in the Custom tab of the item information. Enter in the weight of the HazMat item in the Current Weight box in the custom tab, and in the HazMat Max Weight field on the Purchase Orders & Misc tab, you can enter the maximum weight of the HazMat material that should be used per issue of the item. When issuing a HazMat checked item, TCMax will ask you for the weight issued. When returning the item, TCMax will ask you for the remaining weight of the HazMat item. The remaining weight is then stored in the Custom tab of the tool information using the Current Weight field. If the item is turned in with the difference between the issue weight and turn in weight greater than the value entered in the HazMat Max Weight field on the Purchase Orders & Misc tab, TCMax will let you know that too much of the HazMat material has been used per this issue with an audible “Excessive Quantity” notification. If the Is Disposable checkbox is checked, a second quantity box will appear upon turn-in, asking for the quantity of the HazMat material that was disposed of (not actually used).
This tab tells TCMax® how to process scanned inputs and how to decide whether you are entering an item barcode or an employee number.

There is a menu option under Maintenance titled Create New Item. New items can be created simply by entering an item barcode number that the system does not recognize. A second way to create a new item entry is to click the Create New Item menu option (or hit the F3 key). When you click it, TCMax looks in the database for the next available barcode number and then creates the new blank item with this barcode number. CTRL-F3 uses the secondary numbers that you see above. The top two boxes of this preferences screen tell you what that next barcode number will be. The prefix can be alpha/numeric. The default is blank. The suffix must be numeric. If you want your item barcode numbers to be all numeric then leave the prefix box blank. If you want your barcodes to be six digits long but want to start with the number one thousand then you should enter 001000 in the suffix box. If you want to use three digit barcodes and want to start with the barcode number one then you should enter 001 in the suffix box. The secondary prefix and suffix above allow you to generate different barcodes by pressing CTRL and F3 from the main screen. TCMax automatically checks the database entry each time you click the Create New Item menu option, for the next barcode number. This way you can be entering new items from multiple computers and there will be no conflicts. Hit the F9 key and TCMax places the Prefix in the main input box on the main screen so you can type your own suffix. Hitting CTRL and F9 adds the Prefix from the Secondary barcode sequence above.

If you should accidentally click the Create New Item option or decide not to enter it at this time, then you should simply hit the ESC key and the new item vanishes and the next available item barcode number is reset to the old number if possible.
There is also a menu option under Maintenance titled Create New Employee (F4). It works exactly as new item barcode numbers above.

Do NOT use this mode unless you absolutely must! Check the first box if you have employee ID card barcodes that have the same number of characters as your item barcodes. The only disadvantage with this mode of operation is when you are checking in items you will have to enter an employee and location BEFORE you can turn-in an item. If you should scan an item without first identifying an employee, TCMax® will assume that you are trying to enter a new employee barcode and will respond “New Employee”. Hit Esc to cancel the new employee request. The advantage of this mode is that your items and employee ID cards can all have any length of characters. TCMax® will simply always expect that the first thing you will scan will be an employee number. The second is the location. And as long as an employee number remains on the screen, any other scan deals with the issue or turn-in of an item.
documents.s: Allow ID Cards and Item barcodes to be the same length

documents.t: These two boxes allow you to tell TCMax the first character style of all employees. Checking the top box causes anything scanned that’s first character is a number between zero and nine to be recognized as an employee. Anything beginning with an ‘a’ to ‘z’ or ‘A’ to ‘Z’ is an item. Checking the bottom box causes TCMax to recognize the opposite, that is anything beginning with an alpha character must be an employee and anything beginning with a number must be an item. This mode of operation fully maintains all computerized automation and is OK to use.
documents.s: Use these to base Employee vs. Item on first character

documents.t: If you have not checked the upper checkbox or either of the two between the dashed lines, then you are allowed to specify the number of characters in your ID cards. You can have four lengths of ID cards. The number of characters in the ID cards must NOT be the same as any of your items. In this mode of operation, when anything is scanned TCMax® counts the characters. If the length matches any of the numbers in these four boxes, then TCMax® assumes it is an employee. Anything else must be an item. In this mode of operation, if you don’t have an employee on the screen, and you don’t have the first tab’s Second Person Required to Turn-In Items box checked, and you scan an item, then TCMax® assumes you want to turn the item in and does so.
documents.s: Employee ID Card #1, Employee ID Card #2, etc. The Best Mode

documents.t: To check the number of characters in any barcode, click in the box in the lower left corner of this tab. Scan the barcode and the character count will appear to the right of the box.
documents.s: How many characters are in your ID cards or item barcodes?

documents.t: Use this option when you use US Military ID cards and have a 2-D barcode scanner. It makes both front and rear barcodes equal. If you check this box then make ID Card #3 equal 15.
documents.s: Use first 15 digits of ID card only, US Military

documents.t: We have found some US government ID cards that have the first character on the front and back different. Should you have this problem then check this box and set ID card #3 or 4 to the value 14.
documents.s: Use 2 – 15 digits of ID card only

documents.t: If your employees ID barcodes and your item barcodes are the same length you must check the first check box. The next two boxes are better if they fit your numbering scheme. (Default mode) If your employee ID barcodes and item barcodes are a different length then enter the number of characters in the employee ID card and leave both of the upper check boxes NOT checked. New copies of TCMax® are shipped with this mode enabled and expect 5 characters or 2 characters in an ID card, and 18 or 21 characters like a US Military ID card

There are thirteen tabs; General Requirements, General Req 2, 3, 4 & 5, Company Information & License Password, ID Card and Item Barcodes, Tool/Item Captions, Captions 2, Employee Labels, Item Labels, Courses, and Custom. General Requirements, General Requirements 2, 3, 4, and 5 are the first five tabs. These first five tabs offer a number of options. All of them are local in nature. Changing one option does not affect other computers on the network.

All item captions on the screen, in reports, and on printed labels are fully customizable by you. Looking at the selections above you will see the default captions. If you want this item to print on the item labels click in the Print on Label check box. Note that only a few captioned items are available for print on an item label.

Fields 15 and 18 can also be used to play a .wav file. As an example, one customer has a “52 Card” inspection signature due on certain items. Edit the “TMDE” caption to “52 Card”. Create a wave file titled “TMDE.WAV” and make it say whatever you want i.e. “52 card signature required” and save that wave file into your TCMax folder. Any item that has this box checked on the main screen will automatically have the .wav file played when the item is either issued or turned back in. The other wave file would be titled “CACRL.WAV” and it will play whenever field 18 is checked and the item is issued or turned in.
documents.s: Additional Wave Files can be played for certain items

documents.t: The first time that you run TCMax® you should take the time to set the mode of operation which revolves around the number of characters in your item barcodes and the number of characters in your employee ID cards. TCMax will also warn you that you need to define your printers. The TCMax Label Maker section will explain details of label setup and printer setup. If you are using TCMax preloaded with our default demo data, Start TCMax® by clicking on the TCMax icon on your computer’s desktop. The Log in screen will pop up. Enter your employee number and your password (With the ‘blank’ database type 01 {zero one} for an employee number and 01 {zero one} for the password). The Preferences screen will pop up displaying all of the options. Please use this time to set your printers, at a minimum setting the Page Printer to any laser or ink jet printer that prints on normal sheets of paper. If you are using TCMax with a totally blank database, Start TCMax® by clicking on the TCMax icon on your computer’s desktop. Click on Maintenance and then Log In/Out. Leave the employee number blank, click in the Password box and type “FOD” or “FIRE” to log in. Click on Maintenance again then click on Preferences. The following screen is displayed. Pocket PC TCMax Mobile User Note: Any time that you make a change to the Preferences area you must completely turn off and re-start TCMax mobile on your pocket pc.

It is very handy to have all of your normal ‘work locations’ printed in barcode so that you don’t have to type a work location when issuing assets. Our Label Maker program is capable of printing sets of labels to any printer for your work locations. However, at times it is handier to print a single work location label from here. From the main screen, enter an employee number followed by a work location. Then click the Maintenance/Print a label for the current work location button. From your side by label printer, a label will be printed that has the text of the work location both in barcode and under the barcode. TCMax uses the same label definition as an employee label for this process.
documents.s: Print a Label for the Current Work Location

documents.t: Anyone that is logged into TCMax can generate a Purchase Request. Once generated you can print it, and at that time an Excel .xls and an Adobe .pdf file are generated and saved. In addition to the Purchase Orders table at the bottom of every item you can generate purchase orders or purchase requests. Purchase Requests can be made by anyone logged into TCMax. Click on Maintenance/Purchase Orders & Requests/Create Purchase Request. Select (and filter if you like) items from the upper screen which can display your current inventory or a complete catalog. Items already below minimum order levels will display in red. When you are finished you click the Submit Request button and these items are added to the list visible in the Purchase Orders area and a Purchase Request report will print. At the same time, TCMax automatically creates an Excel .xls file and an Adobe .pdf file of the printed purchase request. You must have permission to enter the Purchase Orders area. Select items for your purchase order from previous purchase requests, your actual inventory, or from a catalog. Add vendor contact information on this screen. Submitting the PO creates a printed report along with a .xls and.pdf file.

Access to the items listed below will only be allowed when an employee “logs in”. Clicking this menu item causes the Permission to Access Screens display to appear. Start typing an employee name and the name will appear. Enter their password. Another password box will appear for you to confirm the password. Be sure to give at least one employee rights to “this screen”, the sixth item down in the list. Once you click Done, an employee with the appropriate access level must login before that feature will be allowed. To login, click on Maintenance/Log In/Out. Enter your employee number in the User Name box and your password in the Password box. The employee that is logged in will appear just above the main input box in the upper left corner of the screen. You can also press the F12 key rather than clicking on the menu. The F12 key will bring up the login box if no one is logged in, it will instantly log out anyone logged in. You can select a .jpg or .bmp picture that will be displayed on the main screen when this employee’s barcode is scanned. Click the Load Employee’s Picture button, navigate to the employee’s photo and double click on it. A copy of the photo will be placed in the directory that is pointed to by the file titled XPath.ini. The first time that you load a photo you will be asked to navigate to the directory where you want to store these photos. On a networked system be sure to place the photos where all users of TCMax can find them.

The database SHOP_CODE field is used to separate data between shops or organizations. When you want to permanently or semi-permanently transfer ownership from one shop to another you can use this screen to transfer single items or multiple items either by scanning the item barcode number or by transferring a number of assets already issued. You first select the top combo box, selecting the shop code that all items will be transferred to. You can enter a new shop code as well. Next you select either an entire shop or you can select from the current list of issued items. So, to prepare to transfer a number of items that you are packing for shipment, you issue those items to someone to a specific work location. Then use the filter combo boxes to select the specific items that are to be transferred. Click the Transfer button and the work is complete. This method keeps all pertinent calibration and inspection data, plus all special certifications intact. You simply copy the database for the receiving organization. If they already have other things assigned as part of a separate database, then you can use the Import screen to pull this data into their separate database. You may also scan or type an item’s barcode number into the green box to transfer 1 item at a time. If you scan the barcode of a parent into this box, the parent as well as its children will be transferred. For example, if you want to transfer an entire kit to another shop, simply scan the kit’s barcode into the green box and the kit, as well as all the components of that kit will be transferred to the shop listed at the top of the screen. When transferring items from this screen TCMax creates a log entry that the shop code was changed as well as who changed them.
documents.s: Transfer Items to a Different Shop

documents.t: This function allows you to be able to issue something and simultaneously transfer it to a different shop. If you are in Issue/Turn In mode and your work location begins with ##, (ex. ##Shop1) when you issue something out to that location TCMax will automatically transfer that item to a shop code of that work location. The ## will be removed from the work location so it will not display on the main screen in the work location box. In order to use this feature you need to be logged in as someone with edit tools permission. This feature will not work with multiple qty items or if you have the preference checked to automatically issue children when a parent is scanned.

documents.t: You begin by entering a master course number in the Barcode Number box, along with the course name in the Item Name box. (Note: we are assuming that you will use TCMax for both item control and for course management. If you are only using TCMax to manage courses of instruction then you can change the captions to fit your needs.) You also must check the Course Requirement check box located on the Purchase Orders & Misc. tab. Remember this course number as it will be used shortly. Now you can add the individual labs and lectures. You do this by: Entering their lab or lecture number. TCMax says “New Item”. You enter the name of the lab or lecture in the Item Name box. Enter the course number in the Parent Barcode Number box. This links this child to its parent barcode number. Check the Course Requirement box. If this item requires more than one hour or more than one session then you enter the number of sessions in the Qty on Hand box, AND you check both Issue multiple of this item with a single scan check box and the Multiple items with this same barcode number box. Both of these boxes must be checked for TCMax to say “Enter Quantity” when completing a course requirement. Put the part number of any item in the table to the lower right along with the number of days before reoccurring training is required and TCMax will automatically assign this item to the Employee Certifications list and certify this employee. Enter zero for the interval and the employee will be permanently certified.

The course requirements mode takes advantage of TCMax ease of use in order to assign a course of instruction to a student and then complete individual entries for that course of instruction with one or two barcode scans. Once your courses are setup you assign a course of requirements to a student by: Scan or enter the student number Scan or enter the course number TCMax says “Yes to issue Children” Click Yes and all of the course requirements are added to this student When a student completes a lab, lecture, or some other course requirement you: Scan or enter the student number Scan or enter the lab or lecture number TCMax may say “Enter Quantity” If it does then you enter the number of hours that were completed Courses can include items that will automatically be certified for that student to use after the course is complete.

You must have permission to adjust student course requirements to enter this mode. Once in this mode all reports revolve around student course requirements and you will not be able to issue or turn in anything that does not have the course requirement box checked.

In normal modes like issue/turn in or physical inventory TCMax will turn something in when scanned if the item is already issued. Many times you want to bring an item up on the screen for display or to edit the item even though you don’t want to turn in the item. Switch to Display Mode and when an item is scanned it is simply displayed on the screen.

Select this mode to quickly update any inspection requirements for any item. When an item is scanned that has a valid inspection requirement the inspection date is automatically updated to today’s date plus the interval displayed for that inspection. If there are multiple inspections assigned to this item then TCMax goes into the Edit mode and the inspections table is displayed. From there you can click on a single inspection and update it by clicking on the Update Selected button, or you can update them all by clicking on the Update All button. The computer’s speakers respond with “Inspection updated”. The Pocket PC version of TCMax works exactly the same way.

When either of these modes is selected, items are NOT issued when scanned. TCMax updates the inventory date or special inventory date in the item table. These dates are reflected in four inventory reports and will show you items that have had and have not had an inventory within a given period. It also updates the quantity in stock. If the item has the “No Turn In” box checked TCMax will ask “Enter Quantity”. The quantity entered will be placed in the “Quantity in stock” value for that item. If the “Multiple items with this same barcode number” box is checked then the quantity in stock becomes the total of the quantity entered plus the total number of these items already issued. If you should make a mistake by scanning something that is not actually there you should scan the barcode again. TCMax will ask you if you if you want to delete the last inventory LOG record, answer Yes and the record is deleted.

This is the normal mode used for all issuing and turning in of anything. Once you switch to another mode of operation you can return to the normal Issue / Turn In mode by clicking this menu option. When you shut down TCMax and re-start TCMax, it always reverts to the default Issue / Turn In mode.

Select this mode to automatically update the current asset odometer reading or hour meter reading. When you scan an equipment barcode, TCMax will ask you to enter the current odometer or hour meter reading. The database is updated and if this new reading causes an inspection to become overdue, the overdue inspection warning is given. The Pocket PC version of TCMax works exactly the same way.

One method used to perform an inventory is to change the “mode” of operation to the Inventory Mode. This does not issue any items. It does update the total quantity of items in stock. You can look at the inventory reports to see items that have or have not been inventoried. A second mode (the preferred method) can be used when all things that you plan to inventory have the same parent barcode number. This works well when inventorying items in a room, building, or all of the items in a single tool box. Scan the tool box number or room number (the parent of all items that you are about to inventory) and issue it to yourself. The Pocket PC version, if in the Physical Inventory mode, will say “Yes to issue Children”. Click Yes. Or with the pocket pc click on the Perform Inventory menu option then the Issue Children of this Item menu option or the Issue Children and Grand Children of this item menu option, answer Yes to the prompt. This causes all of the items in the box or things in a room (children) to be issued and the box or room itself (parent) is turned in. TCMax is taken out of the Issue/Turn In mode and placed into the Physical Inventory mode. The Issued Items screen becomes the Physical Inventory Details/Reports screen where you can print your results. 3. Now you scan the barcodes of everything in the box or room, turning everything in and listening for “Removed” to be played with each barcode scan. When you are complete you can look at the Show items that are out screen. It will show you anything that you missed. Also, if you should scan anything that does not belong in the box or room then TCMax will say “Added” prompting you that it does not belong there! It does this because the item that you just scanned doesn’t have the same parent barcode number as the tool box or room. If you decide to leave the item in this room or box you can immediately scan it again so that you hear Turn In and edit the Parent Barcode Number to the current parent. Physical Inventory does not affect items currently issued. Physical Inventory results are maintained in a separate table similar to the Issued Tools table. When you start Physical Inventory, TCMax will ask if you want to clear old inventory data. Scan the parent barcode then answer Yes to Issue Children. They actually are not issued, just added to the Physical Inventory table. When you scan children they are removed from that list. If you hit something that is not a child of this parent, then TCMax will add the item to the list. When complete this list should be empty. Any item on the list is a problem. Items in yellow are items with the wrong parent. Items with a white background are items that were not found. Again, issuing the children of the parent allows you to quickly issue all items in a room or tool box. Turning them back in one at a time by scanning their barcode is an amazingly fast and efficient way to perform the inventory. TCMax reports the items that you missed or that are unserviceable or missing. TCMax also tells you by saying “Added” rather than “Removed” that an item belongs in another box or room (has a different parent). Expendable (No Turn In) items will issue and be placed in the Issued Items list as well, only when in the Physical Inventory mode. Whenever you “turn in” a quantity that is more than you already have on hand, TCMax will increase the quantity field appropriately. The Pocket PC version of TCMax has this same mode of operation! The Physical Inventory mode, simple example Enter or scan your container number (building, room, vehicle, trailer, tool box, etc.) The computer says "Yes to issue Children?” you click Yes and everything in the container is instantly issued to you Scan every barcode in sight listening to the computer say "Turn In" If the computer says "Turn In", you don't even need to look at the computer screen, just scan the next item's barcode. If the computer says "Issue" than this item belongs in a different container; change the Parent Barcode or move it to the proper container. Scan it again so it says “Turn In”. If the computer says "Enter Quantity", it will display how many of that item should be there. Count them and enter the number that you found. When you think that you are done click the "Show items that are out" screen. Everything that you missed (or is missing) is on this list. That is all there is to it. Performing a complete physical inventory cannot possibly be easier, faster, or more accurate! This works the like the Issue/Turn in mode except when scanning an item that has the Issue Multiple and Multiple barcodes menu options checked. In this case TCMax says “Enter Quantity” as it would in the issue/turn in mode. However, in the issue/turn in mode it always prompts you with the number one (1) guessing that you want one issued. In the Physical Inventory mode, TCMax will prompt you with the quantity of items that it expects you to find at that location, proceeded with a minus symbol. For example, if you have four hoses, TCMax will ask you to Enter Quantity and have -4 in the box. If all four are there you just hit enter. If one is missing then you change the -4 to -3 and hit enter. The Physical Inventory mode was designed to quickly issue everything in a building/trailer/truck/tool box with one click. Then you scan everything in sight, listening for “Turn In” confirming that the item was found in the database correctly. If an item is in the wrong location (has the wrong Parent Barcode number) then you will hear “Issue”. When an item has the Multi tool box and Issue Multiple boxes checked then you are prompted with “Enter Quantity” and the correct number of items already in the box ready for turn in. The goal was to make physical inventories as fast and accurate as possible.

The End of Shift inventory mode allows you to quickly scan ‘holes’ on your equipment shelves to make sure everything that is not on the shelf is actually issued to someone. Click the Mode = menu option and select End of Shift Inventory mode. TCMax will ask you if you want to clear old inventory information. If you answer Yes then the End of Shift table is cleared, then everything that is currently issued is copied to the end of shift table. Then you walk around your tool room scanning the barcode of everything that is NOT on the shelf, removing it from the list. When done there should be nothing left on the list. Items that were scanned but not in the issued tools list will be added to the End of Shift list highlighted in yellow. Items that are considered issued, but were returned without turning them in will remain on the list. The End of Shift mode can be run on one machine while other networked machines continue to issue and turn things in. TCMax will keep all of that straight so there is no longer any reason to shut down your tool room during an end of shift inventory.

Select the Receive Inventory mode when you are receiving existing items into stock. When you scan or type a barcode TCMax will respond with “Enter Quantity”. This quantity will be added to the value already in stock and the computer will say “Inventory”.

From the main screen, click the Edit button on the upper right of the screen. Click in the curriculum box and type or paste your curriculum. Hit the F5 key to save it.

Start TCMax and log in. The person logging in must have permission to complete student course requirements. To enter a completion for another student you simply scan or enter their student ID number then scan the course barcode as above.

The TCMax database comes setup with (automotive example) 8 groups of NATEF tasks, with from 16 to 64 tasks per group. To complete a task for a student you scan each task one at a time. You can easily re-group each of the tasks to smaller groups so you can complete a number of NATEF tasks with a single barcode scan. The following instructions will describe how to add task groups and reassign the existing NATEF tasks to these smaller groups. To assign a task to a group you put the group’s barcode number into the task’s Parent Barcode number. The TCMax database as it ships for example has eight groups. The first group is Engine Repair and the group has a barcode number of 10110000. The first task in Engine Repair is “Complete a work order using customer information, etc.” with a barcode number of 10110010. The second task in Engine Repair has a barcode of 10110020, etc. Each of those tasks has a Parent Barcode number 10110000, matching the group’s barcode number. If you want to add smaller groups so you can complete groups of NATEF tasks rather than completing one at a time you must first add your group barcodes and definitions, then edit the existing tasks, changing from the old major group to the new smaller groups by changing the task parent barcode number. As an example, lets say that you want to add a new group that when scanned will automatically complete the first three Engine Repair tasks. Add a new task group to TCMax by typing a group number that does not already exist, such as 10500000 (additional groups could be separated by tens such as 10500010, etc. ) Remember the number that you assigned to this new group. Enter the proper description for the group and curriculum as necessary to the Notes field. Click the save button, or print a barcode label for this group for future reference. Scan the barcode for the task that is to be reassigned to this small group (or type the number in and hit the ENTER key) Click the Edit button for the task Click in the Parent Barcode number box and enter (or scan the barcode of) the new group task barcode, such as 10500000 as in the example above. Hit the F5 key to save it. Scan the next task, click edit, change the parent barcode number as above and save it. Use this process with all of the tasks, moving them to the smaller groups. Now you can use the TCMax label maker to print barcode number sheets of all of your new groups. To print the master list use the following instructions Start the TCMax Label Maker Load the NATEF Barcodes label definition Click the Print Student Course Requirement Barcodes menu option Either select the individual course names or select the Master Parent List Click the Load Selected Course from Above button Click the Print Labels from Grid button To complete a group of tasks for a student simply scan the student ID then the group barcode. All of its associated NATEF tasks will automatically be marked complete, rather than having to scan each task individually.
documents.s: How to Setup Task Groups or Smaller Groups

documents.t: Start the TCMax Label Maker program Click the menu option that says Items then select Preferences and then Printers and be sure to select a printer that will print to 8 ½ x 11 paper. The Master Parent List set of barcodes appears in the combo box. If you click the Load Selected Course Above button the appropriate information that will create a list of Master Courses will be placed in the Labels to be made table. Then you click the Print Labels from Grid button. To print individual course sets of requirement barcodes, select the appropriate course in the Course Name combo box and click the Load Selected Course Above button. This will cause the course of barcodes to be loaded. Print these, one course at a time.

TCMax has a “Course Requirements” mode of operation designed to streamline the monitoring and recording of NATEF requirement completions. The following instructions are intended to supplement the TCMax user manual. An example of normal day to day use is given first to show you the simplicity of the software. Instructions for adding students and setting up TCMax are provided in later sections of this document. We provide a database with all NATEF requirements pre-loaded. With this database and our TCMax Label Maker you can print sheets of NATEF requirements, ten requirements to a page, with barcodes that when scanned will ‘complete’ the requirement for the selected student. You should use the label maker to print barcodes for your students and the requirements before beginning day to day use. You should also add each student to the TCMax database. Even easier, you can use our Student Maintenance screen to print sheets of instructions for the students that include barcodes at the top. Scan the left barcode then the right barcode and hear TCMax say “Completed” and that task completion is added to the NATEF report. And, if you have curriculum and student assignments created to match groups of NATEF requirements you can create ‘parent’ items with the assignment. Then place the assignment barcode number in each of the NATEF ‘Parent Barcode Number’ boxes. In Student Maintenance you select and print the Assignments. When completed by the student you scan both the student ID barcode and the assignment barcode and TCMax will give credit for all of the child tasks. Optionally TCMax will ask for the grade (proficiency level) that you want to give to the student for this task. Grades are averaged per student and for the school as a whole.
documents.s: NATEF Specific Instructions for TCMax Course Requirements Mode

documents.t: NATEF and other Student Course Requirements Mode TCMax can monitor and report course completion information using the simple TCMax interface to “issue” all of the requirements for a course and (as the student completes each requirement) turn them back in. TCMax can also automatically grant certifications to items and equipment requiring certification when a course requirement is completed. For NATEF (National Automotive Technicians Education Foundation) courses, the reports tell you the percentage of priority one, two, and three items, also telling you if enough have been completed in order to complete the course. Master course barcode sheets and individual course barcode sheets including all course requirements can easily be printed with our label maker program. Certain criteria must be followed when entering course information. Course information and course reports can NOT be entered unless you have entered the Course Requirements mode by clicking on the main TCMax menu item that allows you to switch modes. Also, the logged in employee must have permission from the Employee Permissions and Passwords screen to enter course requirements. As new courses are added (just like adding items) you Enter a barcode number and a course name in the ‘item name’ box. Enter the course code in the “Item Storage Location” box NATEF courses can enter the priority in the NSN box, and it must be in the format “P-1”, “P-2”, or “P-3”. Check the Course Requirement check box for everything within courses. Please note that you may have changed the captions to the three items above, so the Barcode Number is in the top box, Item Name in the third box, Item Storage Location in the fourth box, and NSN in the fifth box. The second box is reserved for the Parent Barcode Number. Do not use the course code for the barcode number! You can, but if you rearrange course codes at a later date students that have already been assigned these codes training will be affected. To issue a course of instruction requirements to a student, again you must be in the Course Requirements mode. Scan or enter the student ID Scan or enter the course barcode number Click the Yes button to issue all ‘children’ requirements As a student completes a requirement to an instructor’s satisfaction, you do the following: Scan or enter the student ID Scan or enter the course requirement barcode number, listening for TCMax to say “Turn in” Non NATEF organizations may have labs and lectures that require a certain number of hours of training. In that case, when you first create the course requirement you must Check the Issue multiple of this item with single scan check box Check the Multiple items with this same barcode number check box Put the number of sessions or hours in the Qty on Hand box When completing these items, you scan the requirement barcode and you will hear “Enter quantity” from TCMax. Enter the number of hours or sessions or whatever the correct quantity will be turned in. NATEF courses have percentage of completion requirements and these are all displayed in various reports. To view these reports you must be in the Course Requirements mode.
documents.s: NATEF and Other Student Course Requirements Mode

documents.t: To add an item to the Lost Items report you turn the item back in if already issued, then issue it to the student or group with the work location “LOST”. When you get a replacement item in you can turn the item back in. The “LOST” record remains. Lost records automatically show up on the Lost Items report, breaking down charges equally between the students. If the lost item is found and you want to remove it from the Lost report then you scan the student’s ID or group ID and enter the word “FOUND” in the Work Location box. Then issue the item to the work location “FOUND”. That will cancel the previous “LOST” action.

Enter an inspection with a description of “STOP-GO” and the following captions appear in the inspections table: The S-G Total Minutes box tracks the total time in minutes that the item was in an issued status. This number of minutes is converted into days and compared to the SG-Max Days Active Service. If the item has more active service (issued status) than the Max Days column, then it is flagged as Overdue Calibration. The S-G 1st Use Days is used to subtract this number of days from the S-G CAL DATE in the Inspections table the very first time this item is issued, just like a WRM item above.

There are a number of DA Form 2062 forms in TCMax, each with a slightly different format. Version two seems to be the most popular. These reports are used to document your property book inventories. The TCMax 2062 expects data to be arranged in a specific manner to be placed properly in the form. The following describes how data appears in the form: Column A, top row, the NSN appears, however we place the Part Number in this same area if the NSN is blank. Bottom row, if the item has a Serial Number then the LIN (CACRL number field) goes here, with no serial number this area is blank. Column B, Name of the item, serial number, and storage location. Column C, Starts off as “D”. If the CACRL box is checked or the item has a LIN, this field changes to “N”. If the item is marked as a throw away item (Do not turn in is checked) then the field becomes an “X” Column D, is a “U” unless the PRECIOUS_METALS field (used to identify classified items for the Army) then it becomes a “7” Column E, the unit of issue from TCMax, and we don’t truncate this. Column F, the Max in Stock goes here, and if max in stock is zero then we display a “/”. Column A, quantity, and if the quantity in TCMax is zero we display a “/” The top row of the form information comes from the “Change Commander Information” button on the Military tab of the Other reports screen.

WRM equipment is calibrated equipment that gets an extended calibration due date as long as the item is not used. As an example the calibration lab may assign a 520 day calibration cycle. Then if the item is placed in use the calibration cycle would be something much shorter like 90 days. Setup, place a single inspection in the item’s inspection table. The inspection description must say “WRM”. Place the actual storage calibration due date in the Date Due Inspection column. Place the interval of the real calibration in the Interval Days column as shown below: When the item is issued, next TCMax will say “Attention” to warn you that the Calibration Due Date is about to be updated and offer the opportunity to cancel this operation. If you say OK then the inspection is deleted and the new calibration date is based on today’s date plus the number of days in the interval column.
documents.s: WRM Extended Calibration Dates for Equipment in Storage

If you don’t want certain issued items to appear in the report simply add their employee number to the Filter: Remove These Users from Report table or add their current location to the Filter: Remove These Locations from Report table. To quickly see all items that are issued (remove the filter) click on the Stop Filter button. This temporarily removes the filters and displays all items. Click the button again REVERSES the filter, meaning that you now only see those items that are listed in the filter boxes. Clicking the button again causes the original filter to be immediately restored. Once you enter employee numbers and/or locations you must click the Refresh Table button. You can also assign colors to your work location filters. If you would like your broken items to show up highlighted in yellow, simply double-click in the color row for the appropriate filter and choose the color from the window that pops up. A new grid will appear listing the components of that parent/kit. Use this option any time that you change options from within TCMax such as the number of characters that you recognize as an employee number or security options. documents.t: With the PC version of TCMax you simply hit the ESC key to clear the screen. In the Pocket PC version you click on the Edit button, and then click the Clear Screen option. The item and employee will instantly be removed from the screen.

Click Edit then Edit Storage Location on the menu at the bottom of the Pocket PC screen. A message will appear at the top of the screen telling you to enter the new storage location. You can do this with the input panel, followed by hitting the enter key.

As with TCMax, the pocket pc version requires you to have permission before you can add new employees or new items. The screen size of the pocket pc is very limited. For this reason we limit the amount of information that you must enter for any new item to barcode, item name, part number, and storage location. When you enter an unknown employee number or item number you will hear the “New Item” or “New Employee” audio prompt and the screen will show a message box asking you if you want to add this new item or employee. Click Yes to start the process. Watch the prompt located just below the text input box. This prompt will tell you what you need to enter next. Once entered you can enter the employee or item number again to continue your item issue process. When a new item is entered you will be prompted to enter the name/description of the item, part number, storage location, quantity on hand, parent barcode number, and whether it is expendable or not.

You can edit storage locations, inspection dates, add new inspections, calibration due date, and parent barcode numbers by clicking Edit and the appropriate menu item. This allows you to edit the information for the current item. Use this when you move something from one parent location to another.

documents.t: The Pocket PC version of TCMax operates in nine different modes Issue / Turn In Physical Inventory Inspection Update Display Status Physical Inventory & Inspect Update Issued Items Inventory Inventory Receive Inventory End of Shift Inventory Odometer Update Course Requirements You can switch to a different mode by clicking on the menu Mode = then click on the appropriate mode of operation.
The issue / turn in mode is the default mode that works exactly like TCMax for the PC. Scanning items results in issuing or turning in items.

This works the like the Issue/Turn in mode except when scanning an item that has the Issue Multiple and Multiple barcodes menu options checked. In this case TCMax says “Enter Quantity” as it would in the issue/turn in mode. However, in the issue/turn in mode it always prompts you with the number one (1) guessing that you want one issued. In the Physical Inventory mode TCMaxMobile will prompt you with the quantity of items that it expects you to find at that location, proceeded with a minus symbol. For example, if you have four hoses, TCMaxMobile will ask you to Enter Quantity and have -4 in the box. If all four are there you just hit enter. If one is missing then you change the -4 to -3 and hit enter.

To perform your physical inventories scan the barcode of the apparatus/trailer/room/building that you are inventorying. After a few seconds TCMaxMobile says “Issue”. Any item that has children items will give you an additional audio prompt saying “Yes to issue children?” Click Yes. The children issue process may take a few minutes, depending on the number of items in your apparatus. Your ‘parent’ item is automatically ‘turned in’ and all child items are issued. Now, do your physical inventory of the parent item, scanning each child item after you inspect it and find it serviceable. Each time you scan an item you hear Turn in and the item is removed from the issued items list. If you make a mistake and scan something that really is not serviceable, simply scan it again. You will hear Issue and the item is placed back on the issued items list. Certain items will give you the audio prompt “Enter Quantity”. This happens when you have a single barcode that has more than one item assigned to it. It is VERY IMPORTANT to know that to turn in these items and remove them from your list you MUST enter a NEGATIVE number. Positive numbers issue items, negative numbers turn them in. So, if you have 10 couplers in a stack, and you find all 10, enter “-10”. All ten will be removed from the list. Continue this process until you have completed the physical inventory. When you finish anything that was broken, missing, or you missed the item remains issued. Everything that you scanned is turned in. If you scan an item that does NOT belong in this parent item then rather than hearing Turn In you hear Issue. This should prompt you that this item is listed as having a different parent, or is shown in a different parent. You can simply click the Edit Parent menu option and immediately change the Parent barcode number to the number of the parent item that the item is currently in. Now you will always know the current location of all child items (except the ones moved in the last few minutes.)

When you issue a parent TCMaxMobile checks for any ‘children’ that have an overdue calibration, inspection overdue, or items that are still issued and therefore ‘missing’ and warns you with the appropriate red letters on the screen plus audio warnings. To see which items caused the warning click on File/Show Overdue Children. A screen appears showing you each overdue item. To perform a physical inventory you click on File/Perform Inventory and then select from Issue Children or Issue Children and Grand Children, depending on the depth of your physical inventory. Slide the slider on the bottom of the screen to the right and you can see the type of inspection that failed and the number of missing items.

When you select this mode of operation, scanning an item simply updates that item’s inspection due date. Select this mode to quickly update any inspection requirements for any item. When an item is scanned that has a valid inspection requirement the inspection date is automatically updated to today’s date plus the interval displayed for that inspection. If there are multiple inspections assigned to this item then the inspections table is displayed. From there you can click on a single inspection and update it by clicking on the Update Selected button, or you can update them all by clicking on the Update All button. The computer’s speaker responds with “Inspection updated”.

This is a combination of the Physical Inventory mode and the Inspection Update mode of operation. An example for its use is to inspect a building full of fire extinguishers. The inspection update portion works as above and the physical inventory portion ensures that you have not missed an inspection. The asset data should be setup (as in the example) with a building as a parent barcode. Then place the building barcode number in each of the fire extinguishers parent barcode number box. Begin the inventory/inspections by entering the Phy Inv & Inspect Update mode, enter an employee number and a location, enter the building barcode number and click Yes to issue children. Then begin turning in all of the fire extinguishers, completing each of the inspections as you go along.

The Issued Items Inventory mode is designed to perform a quick inventory of items already issued. It displays a list of items currently already issued. Then as you scan the barcode of those items the item disappears off of the list on the main screen and the Inventory Date field is updated. You would synchronize the Pocket PC and take it to the work area where all of the items will be found. Scanning an item that is already issued results in the item dropping off of the table on the main screen and TCMaxMobile says “Inventory” and the inventory date is updated. If you find everything that had been issued then the table on the main screen becomes empty.

Scanning items when in this mode puts today’s date in the Inventory field. Inventory reports are based upon this date. The reports are only available in the PC version of TCMax. It also updates the total quantity of this item if either the No Turn In box or the Multiple items with the same barcode box is checked. If checked, TCMaxMobile will ask you to Enter Quantity. This value is used to update totals. With the No Turn In box checked the quantity entered becomes the new value of the total in inventory. If the Multiple items with the same barcode box is checked then TCMaxMobile will add the quantity entered plus the total number of this item already issued and place the total in the total quantity box. The Receive Inventory mode allows you to automatically add the quantity received to that already on hand. Scan a barcode, TCMaxMobile says “Enter Quantity”. Enter the quantity just received. The Pocket PC responds with “Inventory”. After the next synchronization you will find that the quantity entered was added to that already in stock.

You can update the current location of any item easily. Once you have scanned the item barcode, the item is displayed on the Pocket PC screen. Click on the menu EDIT then click Edit Storage Location and you will be prompted to type in the new storage location. Synchronization will cause this to be updated in the PC. There are four reports in the PC version of TCMax that can give you a list of everything that either has been inventoried or everything that has not been inventoried in any given period.

PPC Sync.exe is required for syncing your device. You can download this from the Soaring Software website and it can also be found on your installation CD. You should perform these synchronization procedures before you take your Pocket PC for TCMax use and every time that you return your Pocket PC to its docking cradle after TCMax use.

Plug your Pocket PC into its docking station and wait for ActiveSync®/Windows Mobile Device Center to complete. Launch the PPC Sync.exe application from your TCMax folder. Select what you would like to sync on the new open window and click Synchronize.

Once the ActiveSync® is completed (after plugging the Pocket PC into the docking station), Launch the PPC Sync.exe application from your TCMax folder. TCMax will then open a new window to allow the user to select which shop codes they would like to synchronize to the Pocket PC. The user selects the appropriate information and then presses “Sync”. The “Sync” button will then change to “Complete” when the process is complete. Once this completes you are free to take the Pocket PC and issue items in exactly the same manner as you do on the PC.
documents.s: After you use TCMaxMobile and have plugged the Pocket PC into the docking station

documents.t: A pocket PC and the new version of TCMax called TCMaxMobile can be used in lieu of a scanner to perform a multitude of tasks including: Issue / Turn in of items and other assets Physical Inventories Inventories and Special Inventories Updating inspection dates of items Operation of the pocket pc and TCMaxMobile is similar to the PC version of TCMax and it maintains the same preferences as TCMax. The screen above shows an item that has just been issued and has a calibration due date that is overdue, causing the Calibration label to appear in the middle of the screen and also firing the “Overdue Calibration” audio warning. There are two other bold labels that can appear on the screen, Missing, and Inspection. Missing appears when you issue a parent that has a child item already issued. Inspection appears when issuing an item that has an overdue inspection, or a child that has an overdue inspection.

These labels are designed to print on plain paper. You can enter your employee numbers and names in the label maker. When running the item control software, rather than typing the employee number in the computer, simply scan your employee name.
These labels are actual size, designed to fit the Avery® 5267 ½” x 1 ¾” return address label. The actual printed label is much sharper than this scanned image.

These would be used for items that change possession in the field. These barcodes need to be entered into the database as items and the format will look like this: h_xxxxxx:P;xxx or hxxxxxx:N;xxx the P indicates part number and the N indicates name. You will replace the x’s after the semicolon with a unique barcode number that does not already exist in your database as an item. The x’s between and : will be replaced with the text that will match either part of name or part number of the item. For instance, Joe is issued item 13579 that has ‘Wrench’ in the description/name and goes out to begin work. Mike comes in and is going to take over finishing the job, Mike is issued the item h_Wrench:N;12345. When he gets out to the job he takes possession of the wrench that was issued to Joe and gives Joe the item with thehWrench:N;12345 barcode. Joe then comes back to TCMax and turns in the h_Wrench:N;12345 item which transfers custody of the actual wrench to Mike who is in the field. The items used for theh items can be anything. You could simply print the barcode and put it on a piece of paper. The point is to have something tangible to swap with the employee already in the field that they can bring back and turn-in using TCMax to show the custody transfer of the item

You can mark an item Broken or Unserviceable with two barcode scans. Make up barcode labels that begin with B_xxxxxxx (used for broken items) or U_xxxxxxx (used to mark things unserviceable, followed by any text you like.) The first character in this barcode is a backward apostrophe and the xxxxxxx means enter any text you want replacing the x’s. a. Scan the item barcode to bring it up on the screen b. Scan the special barcode above If the barcode for example is 'U_Broken Connector' when you scan the second barcode as in b. above this item on the screen will automatically have its Unserviceable check box checked and a Log Note will be generated that says “Broken Connector”. If the barcode for example is 'B_Weak battery', when you scan this barcode with an item already on the screen, the Broken box is checked and a Log Note is generated that says “Weak Battery”. If the barcode for example is 'B_EDIT' then TCMax marks the item Broken and opens the Log Notes box to allow you to enter anything that you want. 'U_EDIT' works the same way but checks the Unserviceable box. If the barcode for example is 'N_EDIT' then TCMax simply opens the Log Notes box to allow you to enter anything that you want without marking it broken or unserviceable. 'N_xxxxxx' places the note made up of the text found after the and also does not mark anything broken or unserviceable. In addition there are User Defined versions of the above items as follows. UDB_NOTE:N:search1;search2; etc. This creates a Log Note exactly like theB_Weak Battery note above, except TCMax searches in the NAME field of the database to be sure that any of the values indicated by search1 and search2 above are actually in the description of the asset. If so then the Broken box is checked and the log note is made (above it would say NOTE). In exactly the same way a barcode of_ UDB_MY NOTE:P:search1 searches for a matching Part Number for the item before marking the item broken and creating the Log Note that in this case says “MY NOTE”. UDU_Another Note:N:search1 creates an unserviceable item exactly like above with the :N: saying look for the search1 text in the description field or do nothing. 's_Returned To Service will remove the broken or unserviceable flags from the item and create a log note that shows the item was “Returned To Service”. 'P_ will generate a record showing that a pre-use inspection was done on the displayed item. Many customers found the previous method of creating an inspection named “Pre-Use” that was always overdue to be a bit frustrating. Now for items requiring inspection before use (such as fall protection) the item can be issued out and while it is still displayed on the screen a `P_ barcode can be scanned which will create a log record affirming completion of the inspection and is visible on the inspection history reports as well as the AF244.
documents.s: Marking Items as Broken and Unserviceable with a Barcode

documents.t: You can also transfer items to a new or different shop code by using a single barcode. In order to use this, you must be logged into TCMax with someone who has permission to add new tools. You can also mark something Broken, Unserviceable, or Serviceable with a similar barcode. To do this the barcode that will be made will look similar to `T_ShopCode:CustomText;WavFile The process would be: Scan the item barcode to bring it up on the screen Scan the special barcode above When creating the transfer barcode you will type the name of the Shop Code that you want the item transferred to between _ and : this can be a new Shop Code or one that already exists. If you have CustomText between : and ; an input box will pop up that information can be typed into that will be saved to a log note. You can also have this barcode play a specified .wav file after the ; TCMax will try to play it but if it cannot find the wav file specified, it will play the “Attention” audio. As an example, scanning the following barcode will transfer the displayed item to the Default shop code, display the input box, and play the wav file named Default.wav. `T_Default:CustomText;Default (the .wav is not needed for wave files) The Custom Text and Wav File are optional, so if you just wanted to transfer an item without the input box or Wav File playing, you just do not include those options in the barcodes you create. Also you can mark an item Broken, add a Log Note, and transfer as above.
