The barcodes are as follows: 'TU_LogNoteTest:ShopCode:CustomText;WavFile same as above but item is marked broken `TS_LogNoteText:ShopCode:CustomText;WavFile same as above but item status is changed from broken or unserviceable to serviceable.

The easiest way to add additional NATEF courses is to contact us and we can setup an import database for you. However, you can also do it yourself. As of this printing, TCMax comes with the automotive set of courses and requirements. If you have a motorcycle course too you can add those course and task requirements. However, you must remember to setup a separate Shop Code for this set of tasks. With a separate Shop Code for each major course, the NATEF report will give you student training status based on their specific course rather than all courses. When you add a NATEF task be sure to enter either P-1, P-2 or P-3 in the priority box, and don’t forget the dash!

Whenever an item or employee is entered that is not in the database, TCMax® opens text boxes allowing the user to enter the new data. Fill in each text box as necessary and press ENTER or TAB to move to the next text box. The new data is stored in the database for future use. To cancel a new item or new employee that was created by mistake, simply hit the ESC key before completely filling out the new item / new employee information. New users to TCMax often hunt through all menu options trying to figure out how to add a new employee. We have made it too simple. Just scan (or type their employee number and hit Enter). When TCMax doesn’t find it, TCMax will say “New Employee” and open a box for you to type their name. Type the name and hit ENTER. You can click Maintenance/Create New Item or hit the F3 key to automatically create a new item with the next available barcode number. Be sure that the next barcode number is properly preset from within Preferences before using this option.

This capability is hidden and disabled unless the user logs in through the Maintenance and Log In/Out menu item in the menu bar at the top of the screen. Once properly logged in, Edit buttons appear in the Employee and Item areas. Once an item barcode number or employee number is entered, the appropriate Edit button is enabled. Clicking on the Edit button opens text boxes over the item/employee data. Make any changes that you want at this time. Press ENTER or TAB to get through the text boxes and the new data is automatically saved. In the Calibration Due Date box, pressing the letter T enters today’s date. Pressing a plus adds one day to the date in the box. Pressing a minus subtracts one day from the date in the box. Pressing an M or a Y adds a Month or a Year to the date in the box. To cancel changes, press the ESC key. You will be required to log in using the F12 key and using your employee number and your password. This is the default mode, requiring you to be logged in to do anything. If you want all security removed you must go into the Employee Permissions screen and un-check all boxes for all employees. Then click the X in the upper right corner to exit the permissions screen. After that, logging in only requires that you hit the F12 key and type FOD in the password box.
documents.s: Editing Item or Employee information, when logging in is not required

documents.t: TCMax has the ability to prevent you from issuing items to an aircraft or any location. In the aviation industry this is used to prevent someone from taking items out to an aircraft that has been cleared to fly. It is accomplished by first creating a fake item barcode that has the word “BLOCKED” as the name of the item, and check the Multiple items with this same barcode number box. Save this item and for your own ease of use print copies of this label to stick near your computers. Both of these things, BLOCKED in the item name and checking the Multiple items with this same barcode number MUST be set for the blocked item to work properly. To block anything from being issued, you enter your employee number, enter the aircraft tail number for the work location, and then enter the “BLOCKED” item barcode number, issuing it to the aircraft. While it is issued you will be allowed to turn in other things from that aircraft that are already issued, but you will NOT be allowed to issue anything else to the aircraft, TCMax will say “Attention” whenever you try to issue something to a blocked work location. To cancel the blocked status simply enter an employee number, the aircraft tail number for the work location, then scan your blocked barcode one more time, turning it back in.
documents.s: How to Block the Issue of Items to an Aircraft Getting Ready to Fly

documents.t: Install fingerprint reader and software. Once you have installed the fingerprint reader and software, go to Preferences > General Requirements 4 and Enable Fingerprint Identification.
documents.s: How to set up Fingerprint Recognition

documents.t: The Lost Items Report appears on the Customer tab of the Other Reports menu option. Items and equipment appear in this report once they have been issued to the location “LOST”. The report uses the TCMax Log entries so the item remains on the report even after the item or equipment has been turned back in. The Lost Items Report separates lost items and equipment between employees so you can use the report to ‘charge’ employees for their losses. If an item or piece of equipment is found after the lost entry is made you simply reissue the item to the same employee with the Work Location of “FOUND”. Doing this will remove the last “Lost” entry in the log. The Course Requirements Mode allows you to assign students to a group. You can issue items and equipment to the group. When an item or piece of equipment is lost the Lost Items Report will automatically charge the correct portion of the value of the item to each student in a group. If the item is later found, be sure to reissue the item to the group with a work location of “FOUND” to cancel the loss for the group. The Show items that are out screen has a button that will appear whenever the person that is logged into TCMax has Database Maintenance permission. The button is titled “Mark item as lost”. You select the appropriate record in the issued items grid then click the Mark item as lost button. The current work location for that item is changed to “LOST” and a LOG record is generated indicating that the person (or group) lost the item. This LOG record causes the item to appear on the LOST report giving you the ability to easily charge personnel for their lost or broken items.
documents.s: How to Charge an Employee or Student for Lost Items

documents.t: Log notes can be created for any item by viewing the item on the main screen and pressing Ctrl+N. To view a report on log notes created for an item, view the item on the main screen and press ctrl+shift+n. Log notes can also be created on TCMax Mobile by viewing an item and selecting edit, then create log notes. TCMax mobile cannot view or edit existing log notes.

1.You also must delete the demo Data in the Database. First you should look in the “Show Items that are Out” screen and write down the barcode numbers of the few items that are currently issued. Exit this screen and simply type the barcode number (and hit Enter) of each item currently issued, this will cause TCMax to say “Turn In” with each one, turning the item in. Next, click on Maintenance/Database Maintenance to display the database maintenance screen. There are twenty or so items loaded as a demonstration. Delete each of these items by clicking in the left edge of the table (this highlights the ENTIRE LINE) and hit your delete key. The line disappears and the item is gone forever. Click in the left edge of the table again for the next item, highlighting the entire line, and hit your delete key. Do this with all of our demo items.

Once the software is installed and preferences are set (see Setting Preferences for the 1st Time ) in your computer you must enter employee and item data. This can be done two ways. Running the TCMax® program, enter employee numbers and item numbers Any employee number that is not in the system causes the New Employee prompt to be heard. If you have logged in, a text box opens allowing you to enter the employee’s name. Press the Escape key to cancel. Type the employee name then press enter. Now you can type the next employee number and name. TCMax® is shipped with a blank database that has preferences defaulting to a 2, 5, 18, or 21 character employee barcode numbers. If you have NOT logged in, the New Employee audio is heard but the new employee text box does NOT open. You must be logged in to enter new employees or new items. Any alphanumeric item barcode number that is entered that is not in the system causes the New Item prompt to be heard. If you have logged in, the cursor moves to the Parent Barcode Number box. Press the Escape key to cancel. Enter the appropriate data in each box then press Enter or TAB. Once you have tabbed beyond the last box the new item will be stored in the database. If you have NOT logged in, the New Item audio is heard but the new item text boxes do NOT open. You must be logged in to enter new employees or new items. You can use the Maintenance/Create New Item menu option for creating new items, or simply hit the F3 key. The second method involves opening the database with Microsoft® Access and entering the data directly. This is not the recommended method. The default location of the database is c:\Soaring Software\TCMax\TCS.mdb. The database is password protected. By default, employees are located in the “My Employees” table. Open the table and enter employee names and employee numbers. Employee numbers MUST (unless you checked the box in preferences that allows the same number of characters) have a certain number digits (the default is two or five) so if you give an employee the number one you must enter 00001. Item information is stored in the STOCK table. Enter barcodes in the BARCODEID field. If you decide to give an item the number one, you must enter something like 000001. Since alpha/numeric barcodes are allowed then there is a difference between 000001 and 0000001. Look at the other field names and you will easily see the type of data you can enter. Make sure that you add the SHOP_CODE field value to match your shop code. This defaults to “Default”. Without the appropriate shop code the item will not be seen by TCMax. You can use our sample Excel spreadsheet found in c: Soaring Software \TCMax\SampleForTCMax.xls. The last ten pages of this user manual will walk you through importing a spreadsheet into TCMax.
documents.s: How do I start entering data into TCMax®?

documents.t: Looking for an item and all of them are already in use? Scan your ID, then a work location that says "Tool Not Available" then one of those item's barcodes. TCMax generates a special LOG record for that item. Now you have permanent records of things that you need based on their non-availability.

It is easy to track broken items. Issue the item to anyone, but in the Work Location box enter the word Broken, upper or lower case. In the Show Items that are Out screen, make sure that the word Broken is listed in the Locations Filtered table in the upper right. You can even make an employee number up for your local item salesman and issue the broken items to them if you like but it is not necessary. When issued to the work location “Broken”, TCMax automatically checks the Broken check box in the lower part of the item information screen. This causes the item to appear on the “Broken Report”. When the item is repaired or replaced and you turn the item in, the Broken check box is automatically un-checked. The broken item remains issued until replaced or repaired. The Show Items that are Out screen or the Broken Report will show you the broken items that currently need attention. A complete history of all broken items is available by running the History of Issue Turn in by Location report, and enter the location “Broken”. You can also open the Show items that are out menu option, select the item that is broken or lost and click the Mark as Broken or Mark Item as Lost button.

When you issue something for a long period such as a pager or uniforms enter a special “location” such as “Long Term” when issuing the item. You can use the TCMax Label Maker program to create such a barcode to save typing it in. So, you enter an employee number, and “Long Term” for the location (or a location that makes sense for your organization), then issue the items. Then go into the Show items that are out screen and enter “Long Term” in a line on the right hand Filters table (See above). The items with this location will disappear from the Show items that are out screen, and they will also disappear from the Employee Log screen if the appropriate Preferences box is checked, the top box below must be checked. In the Show items that are out screen, clicking the Stop Filter button will display all issued items, temporarily removing the filtering action. The colors of the items that are filtered can be changed by double clicking on the color box, then click on the appropriate color in the selection box. These colors appear in the main screen’s CTRL-S items out screen too.
documents.s: Tracking issued items for a long term

documents.t: Enter an employee number. When an employee is displayed, the Log table switches modes and displays all of the items that this employee currently has issued. This greatly speeds the turn-in process as you know immediately if that employee has not turned in all of their items. If you are turning in items, it is not necessary to enter an employee number (unless the Second Person Required for Check In feature is enabled). If you do enter an employee number, you can use this entry to document the name of the person that performed final the check of the items on turn in. The Log table will always reflect an issue to the turning in employee’s number instantly followed by a turn in (employee number of zero indicates the item is turned in).

Type in the location that the item is being taken then press Enter key. The Label Maker program will print barcodes that translate into the locations that you normally use, speeding the item issue process. See page 162 for an example of how to use the Label Maker to print barcodes for your locations. You can also assign an individual “default” location for every employee. To set the default location, enter an employee number and location as directed above. Click the Set Default button next to the Location text box. From now on when this employee’s name is entered the location will automatically be placed on the screen. To unset the default location, simply click the Un-set Default button.

You can create barcodes with special characters in them that TCMax® will interpret as both an employee number and work location. If you format your barcode to read “EmployeeNumber~!@WorkLocation” with the ~!@ special characters separating the value TCMax® will recognize all of the characters before the ~!@ as an employee number regardless of character count and everything after the ~!@ as a work location. If the employee does not exist in TCMax yet TCMax® will add that person with the identifier supplied and give them a name using your New Employee Prefix (from Maintenance>Preferences>ID Card and Item Barcodes) then a dash then the identifier you supplied. So, for example, if your New Employee Prefix is “User” and you scan a barcode that reads 12345~!@Dock 1 and employee 12345 doesn’t exist in TCMax® yet TCMax® will create a new employee named User – 12345 with an employee number of 12345 and display them on the screen with a work location of Dock 1. This person is now ready to be issued items. This feature has been added to TCMax® to make it more versatile for one specific industry. Most places don’t have premade barcodes with an employee number and work location being printed out. It is explained here simply to document that it can be done in case other industries/ customers can gain value from using it.
documents.s: Entering Employee Number and Work Locations in one barcode scan

documents.t: If you work at additional ‘work locations’ and want to create LOG records for each of the work locations, even at the end of the day, enter your employee number and any one of the work locations. Press CTRL-D, a prompt opens up asking you to scan or type a work location. Scan or type the work location, any number of work locations and TCMax® will make new LOG records based on the current list of assets issued to you at this time. Hit Enter or click Cancel to go back to the main screen. Note, this option does not work well with hazmat items as it may show usage.
documents.s: What happens if I work at more ‘work locations’

documents.t: Enter or scan the alphanumeric item number then press Enter. Our blank Database contains a few item barcode numbers, such as 112 (press enter key). a. If the item’s Issue multiple of this item with single scan check box is checked then you will hear the audio Enter Quantity and an input box will appear on the screen asking you how many items you want. Enter the appropriate quantity and press Enter key. When turning items in you enter a negative number (i.e. -2 to turn in two items). b. If the item was shown as stored in the item crib, then the audio Issue is heard telling you that the item is issued to you. c. If the item was previously issued and no one properly turned it in, then the software responds with the audio Turn In telling you that the item has now been returned to the item crib. In this case immediately re-scan the item. The Issue audio is now heard and the item is properly issued in your name. d. If the item that you are issuing is overdue calibration or has a “child item” that is overdue calibration then the Overdue Calibration audio warning is heard. It is followed by the Issue audio if the person the items are being issued to has permission to adjust calibration dates otherwise the item is only displayed. e. If the item that you are issuing has a “child item” that has already been issued (like a torque wrench sent to the calibration lab) then the Caution Item Removed audio warning is heard followed by the Issue audio. f. If the item that you are issuing has an inspection that is overdue then the Inspection Overdue audio warning is heard. That is followed by the Issue audio if the option in Preferences has not been turned on that will stop the issue of overdue items. g. If you have set the warning lead time in Preferences for calibrations or inspections to some number of days other than zero and this item calibration or inspection date falls into the lead time area (but it is really not overdue) then a Calibration Imminent or Inspection Imminent warning appears but you are allowed to have the item. 4. You can issue items in bulk by setting up a bulk issue maintenance procedure as found on page 91 and scanning its barcode. 5. Press Ctrl-P to print a list of items that the current employee has issued. You can also type the word “print” in upper or lower case to print the report. Create a barcode label with the word “print” in barcode and you can print the report by scanning that barcode. 6. After issuing all items to this employee, hit the ESC key to clear out the current employee number.

When you issue an item that has the “Multiple items with this same barcode number” box checked, the program simply issues the item to the new employee without turning in the same item already issued to other employees. Each item is tracked separately. Note that you should not use this feature with items that require calibration or inspections or items that are used on aircraft. If you should scan the same item again against an employee that already has this item issued, then TCMax® will turn this item in for this employee only.
documents.s: Issue Identical Items with same Barcode Number to Different Employees

documents.t: If you should issue items that have this box checked then TCMax® needs to know how many you want to issue or turn in. The program gives you an Enter Quantity audio warning then presents an input box on the screen that asks you to enter the quantity that you want. If you already have at least one of these issued to this employee then enter a positive number if you wish to issue more “3” (issue three more) or a negative number if you want to turn some in “-3” (turn in three). The ‘blank’ database has item number 141, rags, as an example.
documents.s: Issue Multiple Items with a Single Scan

documents.t: Certain items may require that an employee be certified before they can use the items. TCMax allows you to check the Certification before use check box on the Inspections & Misc. tab of items. Once checked, you enter your employee numbers of certified employees via the Certified Employees tab. To enter an employee in the list of employees that are certified to use an item: Scan the item barcode. Click the Edit button to be allowed to edit item information. Click in the box in the upper right of the Certified Employees tab as you see above. Scan or enter the employee number, the employee’s name appears in the table. Enter the date certified and the date that the certification expires. If the certification never expires simply enter a date 30 years from now such as 1/1/2035. To delete employees from the list, first enter the edit mode as in steps 1-3 above. Click in the very left edge of the table, in the column that you see the black arrow above. The entire row is highlighted. Hit the Delete key, and that employee is removed from the list for this item only. Separate entries must be made for every item with a different part number and every employee certified for that item. Employees whose certification has lapsed are highlighted in RED as you see above. When you try to issue an item to an employee that is not certified TCMax responds by playing an “Employee Not Certified” audio warning and the item is NOT issued. The TCMax Course Requirements mode can have part numbers assigned so that when a course is completed by an employee, that employee is automatically certified to use any number of certified items and equipment as defined within that course.

The children tab gives you a quick view of all child items of any parent. When you scan or enter a barcode number, if this item has children you will see a complete list of them here. You can edit the storage location, broken status, unserviceable status, and notes directly in this children tab.

The custom tab contains four checkboxes, six textboxes, and two combo boxes that you can customize to reflect any additional information about your items that you need. You can change the captions of these options to reflect the nomenclature that you need by going to the Maintenance > Preferences > Custom tab.
This tab is where you set up vendors, manufacturers, each item’s quantity settings, and view the inspection table.

When you issue an item that has the “Multiple items with this same barcode number” box checked, the program issues the item to the user without turning in the same item already issued to other users. Each item is tracked separately. Note that you should not use this feature with items that require calibration or inspections or items that are used on aircraft. If you should scan the same item again against a user that already has this item issued, then TCMax will turn this item in for this user only.
documents.s: Issue Identical Items with Same Barcode ID to Different Users

documents.t: If you issue items that have this box checked then TCMax will prompt you as to how many you want to issue or turn in. The program gives you an “Enter Quantity” audio prompt and then presents an input box on the screen that asks you to enter the quantity that you want. If you already have at least one of these issued to this user, then TCMax will default to turn in these items. To issue more of this item to the user click in the box in the issue section of the Multi-item screen and enter the quantity.
documents.s: Issue Multiple Items with a Single Scan

documents.t: If the "No Turn-In" check box is checked of any item, that item is not expected to be turned in. To take full advantage of tracking expendables and making sure you do not run out, you will want to fill in the following fields: Qty: the quantity of the item that currently is in stock Reorder Qty: the minimum number of items required for inventory at any one time Max in Stock: the maximum level for inventory. Any expendable item that falls below the Reorder Qty will appear on the Reorder Report. The Reorder Report calculates how many to order based upon the maximum quantity minus the number in stock. The Reorder Report provides you a quick and easy means to keep the proper quantity of expendable items in stock always. Check the Do Not Reorder box and this item will be removed from the Reorder Report. info Expendable items (No Turn-In box checked) cannot be turned in through Issue/Turn-In mode. If a user brings back expendable items that were not used, you must update the quantity of that item through the Receive Inventory mode.

If you have checked the No Turn-In check box of any item, that item is not expected to be turned in. You will find an example of this with item number 140 in the ‘blank’ database. Three new text boxes open up just above the item check boxes. They are: Qty: the quantity of the item or item that currently is in stock; Reorder Qty: the minimum number of items required for inventory at any one time. Any expendable item that falls below this number will appear in the Reorder Expendables Report; and Max Qty: this number is used as a maximum level for inventory. The reorder expendables report calculates how many to order based upon the maximum quantity minus the number in stock. When you issue an expendable item with an employee already displayed TCMax® simply reduces the total quantity in stock, and says the word ISSUE. If you issue an expendable with no valid employee shown, then the item’s quantity text box opens up expecting you to enter the new total quantity that is in stock. This is how you add newly received expendables to TCMax®. The Expendable Items Reorder Report provides you a quick and easy means to keep the proper quantity of expendable items in stock at all times. In conjunction with the Purchase Orders tab you are told exactly what to order and from whom. Items that have the Do Not Reorder check box checked and that have minimum quantity in stock and maximum quantity in stock entered will appear on this report when you are required to reorder the item. You can turn in the expendable items if you wish. Simply enter a negative number when the Issue Quantity prompt comes up. Entering -3 turns in three of the item back into inventory. Enter purchase order number, date ordered and quantity ordered. Once on order, the quantity on order will reflect in the Reorder report. Check the Do Not Reorder box and this item will be removed from the Reorder report.

There are a few ways that an item can be setup in TCMax. The following paragraphs attempt to explain each type of item. A picture of the “Issue Qty & Inspections” tab is displayed for each type of item. Pay particular attention to the check boxes as they define how TCMax will process the item.

No boxes are checked. Use this when only one item has this barcode number. Items like this might be anything taken to an aircraft where if lost you must know exactly which item was lost so you know who lost it and exactly where to search. In this case, if you have several identical items you must assign a different barcode number to each item. When a valid employee is on the screen, if the item is in the crib when scanned then the item is issued. If the item is already issued when scanned then the item is turned in. If already issued to one person, it is turned in even though the employee on the screen is different, and in this case the issue log begins showing you the remaining items that the other employee has issued to them. Examples: Any item going to an aircraft Weapons Radios and Walkie-Talkies Equipment Items Expensive items like skill saws
documents.s: Items that must have a separate barcode for each item

documents.t: No Turn-In box is checked Anything that you want to issue in single quantities. TCMax tracks who received the item and where they are taking it but it does not show up in the issued items screen and they are not required to return it. One is deducted from the Qty on Hand box. If the Qty on hand falls equal to or below the Reorder Qty level then the Reorder Qty turns red. Make an entry in the Max In Stock and Reorder Qty boxes and the Reorder Report will tell you when you need to reorder the item and it will calculate how many to order. Examples: Safety Glasses String for a weed eater
documents.s: Items that are expendable and issued one at a time

documents.t: No Turn-In box is checked. Issue multiple of this item with single scan box is checked. As before, the no turn-in box makes it expendable, the item is issued, logs track who took it and where it went, and it does not show up on the issued items screen. When scanned the Issue Multiple check box causes TCMax to say “Enter Quantity” and a box appears on the screen asking you how many you are taking. Type or scan the number of these you will take and hit the ENTER key. TCMax then says “Issue” telling you that the item was issued. The appropriate quantity is deducted from the Qty On Hand box. Examples: Toilet Paper Lumber Batteries for a flash light Rolls of tap Rubber gloves Rags when you dont want them back
documents.s: Items that are expendable and issued in multiple quantities

documents.t: Multiple items with this same barcode number box is checked. Use this for items that anyone can have, that they can only have one of, and that you want to have returned. When a valid employee is on the screen and the item is scanned, if this employee already has one then TCMax will say “Turn In” and turn the item in, removing it from the Issued Items screen. If this employee doesn’t have one than one is issued to them.] Examples: Helmets Flashlights Pagers Web Belts, Canteens Masks
documents.s: Items or items that you have more than one of but don’t require separate barcode

documents.t: Multiple items with this same barcode number box is checked. Issue multiple of this item with single scan box is checked. Use this for items that anyone can have, they can have more than one, and you want the items returned. When a valid employee is on the screen and the item is scanned, TCMax always says “Enter Quantity” asking how many you want. To issue some, type a positive number, “6” issues six To turn them in, type a negative number, “- 5” turns in five. The items will show up on the Show items that are out screen. Examples: Shirts, Pants, Uniforms Items used in general construction i.e. hammers, wrenches for a bridge builder
documents.s: Items or items that you have more than one of, don’t require separate barcode, but employees can have more than one

documents.t: For items like nuts and bolts that really are expendable but you want to track exactly how many are used on a job such as aircraft manufacturing, check the Consumables box on the Issue Qty & Inspections tab. Then check the Issue Multiple of this item with single scan AND the Multiple items with this same barcode number (as you see above). When you exit the job and are ready to turn in the quantity that you did not use on the job you scan the barcode number and turn in the quantity that you have left to turn in. TCMax will ask you if you consumed the remainder on the job. If you answer Yes then the remainder is removed from the issued items list and a special log entry is made showing that you consumed these. You will also hear TCMax say “Consumed”. There is a special Consumable report.
documents.s: Consumables, for manufacturers that have expendable items consumed in a job

documents.t: Many companies use item chits (plastic or metal tags with an employee number attached) for employees to place in a drawer where an item is taken. There is an item Chit check box on the Inspections and Misc. tab. When an employee starts a job they can issue themselves a quantity of item chits. When they end their shift they can turn them back in. Those issues and turn-ins will appear on a special Item Chit report.

If you must perform periodic inventories of items in vehicles, kits, trailers, or shops, you MUST assign a different barcode number for the item for EACH vehicle! For each item, place in the Parent Barcode Number box the barcode number of the vehicle that the items are in. Then when you start the inventory you will: Issue the Parent barcode number, probably the vehicle number. Click the Issue the Children of this Parent menu option 75\ This will turn in the parent vehicle Issue everything in the vehicle Scan all items in the vehicle, turning them in When done, anything missing or broken will appear in the Show items that are out report.
documents.s: Items in vehicles and performing their inventory

documents.t: If you have not already selected a picture and you enter a part number, upon exiting the part number field TCMax will try to pick a picture of the item from the catalog database. Otherwise click the Set Picture button and navigate to the picture of the item. A copy of the picture will be placed in the c: Soaring Software \TCMax\Catalog_Photos folder or placed in the network folder when you have setup a network path for photos and attachments.

This tab allows you to document other information for your items. You can type in any additional information for your items in the Notes section as well as record the length, width, height, and weight for the item if you choose to do so.

With expendable items (no turn in box checked) we have always allowed you to set minimum/maximum in stock and warn you when you are below stock. Now there is a new Min/Max by Part Number check box that affects non-expendable items, tools, equipment, etc. when you have a part number assigned. The Quantity on hand will show its normal quantity (usually 1) but the Qty Available will show the total of that part number that you have, and it will say Attention as a warning when the Qty Available goes below the reorder limit based on the others being marked broken or zero Qty on hand.

This software provides you the capability to print complete packing lists including total weight and cube for the increment or pallet. If you have taken the time to place height, length, width, and weight in each of your equipment’s item entries then use the following process: Assign an “employee number” with the name of your deployment. Enter the pallet number or increment number that you are putting the equipment item on, in the “Location” block. Issue all equipment as it goes out the door to be loaded on the pallet. Run the Items issued to a particular employee grouped by location report. It will sort all equipment by increment number, each increment getting a separate page. The total weight and cube will be found on the bottom of the report. Use the Transfer Items to a Different Shop menu option to permanently transfer assets to a different shop code.
documents.s: How to use Packing for Mobility

documents.t: Whenever a parent item is issued that generates an overdue or missing warning due to one of its children, a Show Child Details button appears in the lower left portion of the item information area. Clicking this button causes the item log grid to display a list of all of those items that caused the warning. Any item with a user employee number caused the missing warning to issue. Any item with a calibration due date that has passed, caused the overdue calibration warning.

Items can be assigned a parent barcode number. As an example, let’s say you have a torque wrench (barcode number 114 in the ‘blank’ database) that you store in an itembox (barcode number 120). If you put the toolbox’s barcode number 120 in the Parent Barcode Number box of the torque wrench, you now enable two features whenever the parent is issued. If the torque wrench is overdue calibration, issuing the toolbox causes the Overdue Calibration audio to be heard, followed by the Issue audio. If the torque wrench has been issued which would happen if you send it to the calibration lab, issuing the toolbox causes the Caution-Item Removed audio to be heard, followed by the Issue audio. You can have an unlimited number of child items in any container. Appropriate warnings will be given if any item is missing or overdue calibration. Again, a container (tool box, ambulance, CONEX, building, etc.) has a barcode number. Items have their barcode numbers. For any items that are located within the container, place the container’s barcode number in each item’s parent barcode number box. Do not put any numbers in the container’s parent barcode number box.
documents.s: Setting up Parent-Child Relationships with Items

documents.t: Rags, issue them for use. Turn them in and some are dirty. Take dirty rags and reissue them to the laundry. Clean rags come back from the laundry and are ready for use. These are the steps, here are the details. TCMax uses the Rag checkbox on the Purchase Orders and Misc. tab of the main screen to spot rags. The caption for that checkbox must say “Rags”. The Set USAF Defaults button in Preferences will set this caption properly. Rags that are not clean and ready to use are managed in our issued items table in the Show Items that are out screen.
documents.s: How to Issue / Turn In Rags

documents.t: Enter an employee number Enter a work location such as an aircraft tail number Enter the rag barcode, TCMax will say ‘Enter Quantity’ Enter the number of rags that you are taking in a positive number

Enter an employee number Enter a work location or leave the work location blank Enter the rag barcode, TCMax will say ‘Enter Quantity’ Enter a negative number, turning in your rags a. TCMax will ask how many are ‘dirty’ TCMax will automatically reissue the dirty rags to a work location of “DIRTY RAGS”, using the name and employee number of the person running TCMax.

Enter your employee number Enter “LAUNDRY” in the work location box Enter the RAG barcode, TCMax will ask you to ‘Enter Quantity’ Enter the number of rags going to the laundry in a positive number TCMax will “turn in” that many dirty rags then reissue them to the work location “LAUNDRY”

Enter your employee number Enter “LAUNDRY” in the work location box (make yourself a barcode that says “LAUNDRY” to save time Enter a negative number, the number of rags returning from the laundry (i.e. if 45 come back from the laundry then enter -45, subtracting 45 rags from the issued items list). TCMax will automatically turn in the appropriate number of rags that were previously issued to the laundry.
Start the program by clicking (or double-clicking) on the TCMax® icon.

The ‘blank’ Database contains a few employees and requires that you log in before issuing or turning in items. Hit the F12 key (if the login prompt is not already there) and type an employee number and password to log in. The upper left corner of the screen will display the name of the logged in employee. All you need to do to check out an item is: Enter an employee number Enter the location that you are taking the items Enter the item number(s) If you have installed an optional thermal receipt printer then you can press Ctrl-R to print a receipt containing a list of the items that this employee currently has issued. The receipt will automatically print whenever you clear the screen, press Ctrl-R, or switch to a different employee. The table in the lower left portion of the screen displays the list of items issued to the current employee. If this employee is turning in items that belong to someone else then the table displays the list of items that are issued to that employee. The table can also display a list of expendable things that the current employee has ever had issued. Press Ctrl-L and the table will switch display modes.

To check in an item, all you need to do is enter the alphanumeric item number. (Optionally, if you first enter an employee #, the item will be assigned to that employee then immediately assigned to no one, to track who turned it in. Also, while turning in items, if the employee number is first entered then the Log table switches to display the list of items that are out. This helps spot items that the employee failed to turn in … optional). If you happen to be turning in someone else’s items, then after turning in the first of their items the table will display the list of items still issued to the OTHER person helping to show you if they forgot to give you all of them. Entering the employee name on turn in also can be used to document the person performing the turn-in item inspection. Note the screen above; the data input box in the upper left of the screen must be either yellow or green before you can turn in items. If it is light red then you must login before you can do much of anything. Items that have the Issue Multiple and Multiple Items boxes checked as you see below may require a slightly different turn in process. TCMax must know whose items you are turning in. If you are turning your own items in and your employee number is on the screen then TCMax will automatically turn yours in. If you are turning in someone else’s items, AND you have already turned something of theirs that doesn’t have these boxes checked, then TCMax assumes that you are turning in things issued to the other employee, and turns theirs in. If you are turning in someone else’s items, AND you have NOT already turned in something of theirs, then TCMax must ask you who’s items you are turning in. It does so by displaying the following screen and says “Please select employee”. The screen displays everyone that has the item that you are attempting to turn in. Click in the row of the person/location that had the item and click the Turn in items from selected row button.

You can turn in all items that a specific employees has, or all items that were taken to a specific location, with a single barcode scan. You begin by creating two barcodes that within the barcode say “returnloc” or “returnall”. Save these barcodes. To turn in all items held by a specific employee, scan the employee number, and then enter their work location. Scan the “returnall” barcode. TCMax will tell you how many items this employee has and ask you if you want to turn them all in. To turn in all items taken to a specific work location by a number of employees you scan the employee number, scan or enter the work location then scan the “returnloc” barcode. TCMax will tell you how many items it expects and ask you if you want to turn them back in.
documents.s: Additional turn in options to turn in multiple items in a single scan

documents.t: TCMax generates a record in the LOG table each time you issue or turn in an item. Those records create a history of item and equipment usage that is available in TCMax reports. TCMax will automatically erase an issue LOG record if the item is turned in within 60 seconds of issuing the item. In this way usage records are not generated when an item is accidentally scanned by mistake then turned immediately back in.
documents.s: Item Issue Records, what happens if I scan an item by mistake?

documents.t: When you are installing TCMax for the first time you will be asked what type of database you wish to use. You will want to select Blank Database. Once TCMax has been installed the very first time you run TCMax you will be taken to the Preferences screen to set up your printers. The first things we will do to enable Evidence Tracking will be done from this Preferences screen. If you’ve already run TCMax and are looking to enable Evidence Tracking you can log into TCMax either with the login you’ve created or with the default 01 employee number and 01 for the password. The first place we should go is Maintenance> Preferences. You will want to locate the arrows on the top right of the window. Hit the right arrow a few times until you see the Captions 2 tab. From the Captions 2 tab Click on the {POLICE} button to reassign the captions on the main screen to be more appropriate to the tasks you will be performing. Once you’ve done that click OK and you will be taken back to TCMax’s main screen.

TCMax differentiates between people and things by character count. When you first logged in you used an employee number of 01. That is two characters, the 0 and the 1. In the Preferences area TCMax is set up by default to know that if you input 2 characters you are dealing with an employee. There are four character counts total that you can associate with employees. By default those values are 5, 2, 16, and 18. This means that if you type in a value or scan a barcode with 5 characters TCMax knows it’s an employee. If it has 16 characters, TCMax knows it’s an employee. 18 characters…employee. Any other character count will be considered an item instead of a person. These values can be changed by you at any time but you really want to decide how you’re going to identify yourselves from the start and stick with it. Otherwise you’re going back and reworking your data which is not necessary if you plan properly. It is recommended that you find some sort of identifier that all personnel have (for example, a badge number). You simply want to find a universal character count that can be used to identify your people. If your badges typically have 2 characters in them, for example, 73 but you have an employee with the badge number of 6, simply enter them into the system as 06, this way it is still 2 characters. To alter the amount of characters TCMax associates with employees simply go to Maintenance>Preferences and click on the ID Cards and Item Barcodes tab. At the bottom of that page you will see Employee ID Card#1 – 4 as seen below. In the above setting we’re telling TCMax that 2, 5, 16 and 18 are going to be employees, every other character counts will be considered items. As an example, if you want to use a 4 character value to identify your employees (last 4 of SSN or phone number, etc) simply change the value in one of these boxes to 4. If you’re certain that you want to use 4 and only 4 characters to identify your people you can put 4 in all of these boxes or 4 in one and 0 (zero) in the rest as seen below. This way all other character counts are open to be considered items. While you’re on this preferences tab go to the top of the screen and find the Employees Prefix and Suffix area. This area allows you to tell TCMax how you want to auto-number people. Your law enforcement personnel will have a badge number which you can use to identify them but when property owners come to claim their personal items you will want TCMax to assign them a number. It’s not important what the number is; only that it is unique so you’ll be able to reference the transaction of returning their property to them at a later date. In the example above, we’re telling TCMax we want 4 characters to be considered an employee. It is important that whatever we put in the Employee Prefix and Suffix adds up to a total of 4 characters. Put an “A” in the Employee Prefix and in the Employee Suffix type “000”. When you tell TCMax to automatically generate a number it will generate the number “A000”. The next time you tell TCMax to generate an employee number it will generate “A001” then “A002” etc. The prefix you set can be alpha/numeric but the suffix must be numeric because TCMax will automatically increment by 1 each time you create a new item. This way every new employee gets a unique number. The nice thing about using this A000 numbering system for your property owners is upon first glace you’ll be able to tell that this person was a civilian because of the preceding “A”. If their number was “2423” you can assume that is some sort of law enforcement badge number. Again, you are not forced to use a 4 character identifier for your employees/personnel as I’ve shown in this walkthrough. The important thing is that you use a character count that is constant so your people don’t conflict with your items. Once this is set up, you shouldn’t have to change it. The instructions on the next pages will give you a step by step guide to adding new people once this preferences area has been set up.

TCMax uses Work Locations during the issue process to help you track where your evidence is going when it leaves your evidence room. If you would like to add additional common work locations (forensics lab, court, etc) from the main screen of TCMax go to Maintenance>Preferences and click on the Gen Req 5 tab. Make sure the “Display Work Locations in buttons” option is checked and simply add your common work locations to the grid in the bottom left as seen below:

From the main screen of TCMax, in the colored box in the top left, type in the person’s badge number and hit enter. In this example we will use the 4 character badge number of “1234”. If this employee has not been entered in to TCMax yet, TCMax will say “new employee” and the cursor will drop to the Employee Name box. Simply type in this person’s name and click the Save button. You can also assign them an organization and shift should you desire. If you wish to issue something to this person you will have to retype their number into the main input box in the top left and follow the “To issue items” instructions located on the main screen.
documents.s: Adding Law Enforcement Personnel to TCMax

documents.t: From the main screen of TCMax hit the F4 key. TCMax will automatically generate a number for this new person and you will hear “new employee” The cursor will drop to the Employee Name box. Simply type in this person’s name and click the Save button. You can also assign them an organization and shift should you desire. This person has now been added to TCMax. If you wish to issue something to them simply retype their number, in this case “A000”, into the main input box and follow the “to issue items” steps located on the main screen.

Technically TCMax treats suspects the same way it treats the evidence. Suspects should not be entered in as employees. The only employees you should have are people that are signing out or turning in evidence. Tracking suspects the same way you track evidence allows you to easily pull up a case and see all evidence and suspects involved in the case. To add suspects use the following steps: Hold down the control key on your keyboard and hit the F3 key. TCMax will say “New Item” and automatically generate a unique ID number for this suspect. You may notice that the identifier TCMax generates begins with “SUS”. The main goal of this is to allow you to easily identify this item as a suspect just by looking at that number. After hitting the Ctrl + F3 your screen should look as follows: Next you will enter in the suspect’s name in the Item Name field and possibly the suspect’s SSN or contact number if you have it. Enter the “Case Number” of the crime this person is suspected of. You will also notice the “Is Suspect” box in the Custom tab is checked for you. This will allow you to run a report that lists only suspects. When you’re done entering information, your screen should look similar to the following: Once you’re sure your data is correct simply click the “F5 to Save” button on the screen or hit the F5 key on your keyboard. Congratulations, you’ve just added a suspect and associated them with a specific case.

To add evidence to TCMax you must first be logged in as someone who has permission to add new items and use the following steps: Hit the F3 key or go to Maintenance>New Item. TCMax will automatically generate a unique ID number for this item. The right side of the screen, where TCMax stores data on each item, will also be opened up for editing as seen in the screen shot below Type in any relevant data you have for this item such as Case Number, Item Name, Storage Location, Property of, where and when it was collected and who it was collected by. Only put info in the fields you have data for. None of these fields are mandatory but the more you enter, the more use you’ll get out of the information down the road. After you’ve entered all relevant data simply hit the F5 key on your keyboard or click the blue “F5 to Save” button in the top right of the screen. Congratulations, you have just added a piece of evidence. If you would like to print a barcode label for this item simply click the “Print Item Label” button located in the middle-right of the main screen. To add another piece simply repeat steps 1-3.

Once you’ve received orders to return or destroy evidence you can tell TCMax that you will be destroying or returning these items at a later time. From the main screen of TCMax click on the Item Search menu option. Once on the Item Search screen, TCMax should be showing you all the items in your database. Rather than scroll through the entire grid looking for a few specific items, we suggest typing in the Case Number of the items to be destroyed in the Case Number field towards the top of the screen. Once you’ve typed in the Case Number hit the “Enter” key on your keyboard. Now only items/suspects belonging to this case are displayed in the grid at the bottom of the screen. You could filter this grid further by entering in part of the item’s name. If you type the word “powder” into the Item name box, and leave the case number you already entered in that box then TCMax will only show you items that belong to that particular case with the word “powder” in the name field. Once you locate the item(s) you wish to destroy or return simply select them from the grid and click the appropriate button. Either Prepare to Destroy or Prepare to Return. In this example I will be destroying item number 00013. Once I click on the Prepare to Destroy button TCMax asks for confirmation that I indeed intend to mark this for destruction at a later time. If you click “Yes” you will be prompted with another message box asking you to enter any notes you see fit to enter. For example, if you wish to record by whose authority you’re destroying /returning items, you could type in “so ordered by Judge Williams” or something similar. If you do not care to enter notes simply leave that box blank and click “OK”. The same steps apply to marking items as returned. All you’re doing at this point is changing the “shop code” these items belong to and possibly adding a note to explain why you’re doing this. The main function of this step is to allow you to differentiate between your current evidence with trials/investigations that are on-going from the items just waiting to be picked up by their owners or destroyed by authorized personnel.

From the main screen in TCMax, in the colored box in the top left of the screen, type in the ID number of the person that will be receiving or destroying the items and then hit “enter” on your keyboard. TCMax should respond by saying “Employee”. You will then be shown a screen with your common work locations as buttons. Click the Destroyed, or Returned button as applicable. Once you’ve hit the correct button you will be taken back to TCMax’s main screen. Simply type or scan the number of the item(s) you are destroying or returning. Each time you type or scan an item you should hear TCMax say “Issue”. Once you have finished issuing everything to this person hit the F6 key on your keyboard to begin the signature capture process. A window will appear with the transaction details on it. On your LCD Signature Pad you will also see the transactional data. The first signature will be the person that is doing the issuing. This is your Evidence Room Attendant and will be the person who is logged in and operating TCMax. Once that person has signed and clicked ok on the signature pad you will be prompted to have the person receiving/destroying the items sign. Their name will also appear on the signature pad. Once they’ve signed they can click “ok” on the signature pad and the transaction ends. You will notice that a spreadsheet opens and the transaction data is placed into the spreadsheet along with the two signatures. The spreadsheet will automatically close itself and saves to whatever folder you told it to save to during setup.
documents.s: Destroying or Returning Evidence in TCMax

documents.t: There will be times when people come in to have their property returned to them or a detective is looking for a specific item. At these times you may not always know exactly where every item in your inventory is. TCMax has made finding these items very simple. Just use the following steps: From the main TCMax screen, go to the Item Search menu option. The bottom half of the Item Search screen contains a grid with all of your suspects and evidence listed in it. The top half contains filters for you to narrow down the results visible in the grid at the bottom. If you have 5,000 pieces of evidence you won’t want to be digging through the grid to find the one you’re looking for. Simply use the filters up top to narrow down your search field. In the screen below we see an example Item Search screen. You can see that you can search by ID Number, Case Number, Name, Location, etc. If someone were to come in asking for an item that belonged to case 08-0003N you could type that into the Case Number box up top and only items associated with that case number would be displayed at the bottom as seen below: In this example we only show 2 results associated with that case. It is now much easier to find the evidence we were looking for as we only have 2 choices and can see the storage location of both items is Shelf 1. You can resize any of the columns in the grid at the bottom as well as sort the grid by each column. If you would like to sort this grid alphabetically by name simply click on the column header (the actual words “Item Name”) and TCMax will sort the grid A-Z by based on the item’s name. If you click the same header again TCMax will reverse the sort to Z-A based on the item’s name. Another useful item on the Item Search screen is the “Show Pending Items Only” checkbox. Checking this box will only display records in the grid that are not currently issued out.

In another example, we’ll search for suspects. From the Item Search screen simply type SUS in the ID Number box up top. Because of the stored procedure within TCMax to automatically number your suspects with the SUS prefix, when we come to Item Search we can simply search for any ID Numbers containing SUS and only our suspects will be returned as seen below: You may notice that we have suspects from many different cases displayed. If you wanted to narrow down suspects to one specific case, simply add that case number in to the filter up top as seen below:

There are a few things to be aware of concerning all reports. The majority of TCMax reports can be found by going to Other Reports from the main screen. On that Other Reports screen you should notice some time and date filters in the top right corner as seen below: When running reports that are dealing with historical data you can change the time/date range that TCMax is populating the reports from. You may want to run a “history of issue/turn in by Employee” report which will show you every item a particular individual has been issued. If you ran that report with the time/date filters shown above the report would list every issue/turn in that employee has had within the last calendar year. If you were only concerned with the issue/turn-ins this employee had during the last week, you could change the date range box’s value from “Year” to “Week”. You could also put in exact times or dates to refine your searches by. Another thing to keep in mind concerning the Other Reports screen is your ability to export the report data into a PDF or Excel Spreadsheet. Towards the bottom of the Other Reports window you will see a check box for “Create Report.pdf & .xls when report closes”. If you check this box and run a report TCMax will create 2 files named Report.pdf and Report.xls. The location where TCMax stores these files is set up by you the first time you try to save a PDF or Spreadsheet. If you forget where you set these files to save you can click on the About menu option from TCMax’s main screen. At the bottom of the About window you will see “Path to report pdf files”. This is the location TCMax is saving these files to. It is important to note that each time you do this TCMax will create a Report.pdf and Report.xls so if a previous Report.pdf exists it will be replaced by the new one. If you want to keep one of the Report.pdf or Report.xls files you will want to navigate to that folder and rename it before you try to export another report.

There are two reports that have specifically been added to help with Evidence Tracking. The first can be found by going to Other Reports from the main screen in TCMax. On the Other Reports screen, click the Special tab and the last report on that tab is the Shop Code Transfer Report. Running this report will show you a history of items that you have marked as needing to be destroyed or needing to be returned to owner as seen below: In the above report we can see the date items were marked as needing to be returned/destroyed, who did the transfer, the reason for the transfer as well as other useful information. The other report specific to Evidence Tracking is located in Other Reports and is at the bottom of the Customer tab. The report is named Police Property Receipt. This is basically a chain of custody report. When you click on this report an Enter Data Here box appears at the bottom of your screen. Enter in the ID Number for a specific item or enter a case number for all evidence associated with that case. Either way TCMax will return 2 reports. The first will be a listing of all items in question. If you run this report for one specific piece of evidence only that piece will show up on the first report. If you run this report for an entire case, all evidence associated with that case will show up as seen below. Once you print or close the above report a second report will come up. This second report contains the transactional data for all the evidence in this case as seen below: The above report shows all transactions for evidence belonging to case 08-0002N.

Should a signature ever be contested or need verified you can log in to TCMax and from the main screen go to Maintenance>Verify Signature on Excel Spreadsheet. Each time you capture a signature TCMax creates an Excel Spreadsheet containing the transaction data as well as the signatures. Once you click the Verify menu option you will be asked to locate the transaction in question. On your Chain of Custody report you will see the date of the transaction as well as the person who has signed for custody of the item as seen below: The signature you would be looking for on the above transaction will be named Patrick McDevitt 3-31-10 and then the time it was captured. The location where TCMax stores these files is set up by you the first time you try to save a PDF or Spreadsheet. If you forget where you set these files to save you can click on the About menu option from TCMax’s main screen. At the bottom of the About window you will see “Path to report pdf files”. This is the location TCMax is saving your signatures to. Once you’ve located and opened the signature spreadsheet from within TCMax you will see a screen similar to the following: The spreadsheet is double-encrypted and cannot be altered. Should the contents of this spreadsheet change for any reason the signatures will no longer be visible until the spreadsheet is restored to contain the correct data.

Keys to storage facilities require that someone else be logged into TCMax other than the person that is getting the keys. Also, when turning those keys back in, the person that they were originally issued to must be on the main screen, and not logged in. User Checkbox number 4 is now used to identify facility keys. If you click the USAF standard options button in Preferences the user checkbox 4 will be captioned “Facility Keys”. When an item has this box checked then the issue/turn in logic above will be applied to that item no matter what other options within TCMax are turned on.

If you have to deploy with another unit that is using TCMax, issue the items that you are taking on the deployment typically to a work location of Deployment or TDY. From the main TCMax screen press CTRL-Z to bring up the TDY Mobility Exporter screen. Select that employee and or work location then click the Export button. A TCMax TDY Database (TDY.mdb) will be generated and stored in the application folder, normally c: Soaring Software \TCMax\TDY Database\today’s date. Take a copy of the TDY.mdb and DatabasePassword.ini files to your deployed location. If they are running TCMax at that deployed location you can simply place the above two files on the new machine, startup TCMax, and hit CTRL+Z. Click the import button and navigate to your TDY.mdb file that you brought with you. You can import more than one TDY.mdb to a host so all of the units’ deployable databases can be imported into one central database.

Inspections can be tracked by the date that the inspection is due, or the miles / hours due. In the example above a date was entered in the Date Due Inspection field of the Inspection Requirements box, along with an interval that will automatically update the inspection date when you are in the Inspection Update Mode of operation. Similarly, you can make a numeric entry in the Miles/Hours Due box. When you enter current Miles/Hours that are greater than the due box, the overdue inspection warning fires. The Inspection Update mode of operation causes the inspection due date or the miles / hours due number to be updated based upon the interval in the table. This screen shot taken February 21, 2008 with both calibration and inspection look ahead set to 45 days. This item is not yet overdue, but within the 45 day period. The screen below was taken in March with both items clearly overdue.

TCMax will print completed NAVSUP Form 306’s based on inspections that have been updated either manually or via the Inspection Update mode. The inspection must have the acronym ATAF in the description, like “ATAF Inspection”. Pressing CTRL-Shift-N will bring up the Navy form 306. The front side of the form is based on issue/turn in history. The back side is based on updated inspections.

As of this writing, USAF regulations require a password or digital signature before you can issue the keys to a munitions storage area. The user checkbox 2 in the TCMax custom fields can be used to ask for the password of the person that is receiving the item. Be sure to setup passwords for all employees that may get keys.
documents.s: Issuing keys to a munitions storage area

documents.t: At the end of every shift it is common for shops to require that you compare your items out list to empty holes on your shelves to insure everything is accounted for. To do this from TCMax you would need to be logged in and the person logged in would need the “switch modes of operation” permission. Once this person is logged in, click on the mode tab up on the top menu bar (the caption will most often be mode=issue/turn in). Click there and switch to End of Shift Inventory Mode. A magenta colored bar will appear across the top of your screen to help remind you that you are in a different mode of operation and you cannot issue or turn in items from this mode. Once you are in End of Shift Inventory Mode simply walk around and scan the holes in your shelves where items are gone (items that are not on the shelf are either missing or issued). Each time you scan something TCMax will say “removed” (removing it from the list of issued items). When you scan an item in Inventory or Special Inventory modes all you are really doing is putting today’s time/date into the date last inventoried field for that item in your database. If you make a mistake and scan the wrong barcode simply scan it again immediately and TCMax will ask if you want to delete the record of that item having been inventoried. Also keep in mind that Special Inventory mode and Inventory mode will both behave the same way and should serve the same purpose. They are two separate modes of operation to allow you to be able to do more than one inventory in the same place at the same time and keep your results separate. If you have a general login be sure to switch TCMax back in to Mode=Issue/Turn In when you’re done so the next shift doesn’t accidentally inventory something instead of issuing or turning in. If a new person logs into TCMax it will default back to the Issue/Turn In mode unless preferences have been set to override this function.
